sh4sqwritesh4sqwrite The SQ WRITE half is never judged -- so an SQ page can raise no initial-page-write and no write-side protection fault, while the PREF still raises the read-side setsh4sqwrite The SQ WRITE half is never judged -- so an SQ page can raise no initial-page-write and no write-side protection fault, while the PREF still raises the read-side set — witness: none yet -- GUEST-REACHABLE and witnessable at rung 3 (a real guest store through real decode, observable in EXPEVT), but a witness needs a build, which the machine embargo forbids. — note: *** SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-08-27: THE DEFECT IS THE **WRITE HALF ONLY**, and saying the window 'bypasses the MMU ENTIRELY' reintroduces wording this row's title was already corrected away from. *** **Why the unqualified form is wrong:** the round's own `sq miss evt` detector observes a **read-type TLB miss (`0x040`)** on the fixed build, so the read side is NOT unrouted. `memory_sh.c:290-301` carries the corrected scope. > **THE CORRECT STATEMENT: no initial-page-write exception and no write-side protection check on stores into the SQ window.** The read/prefetch path translates; the store path does not. That asymmetry IS the defect, and it is narrower and more defensible than 'bypasses the MMU'. **AND THE SECTION CITATIONS ARE BOTH RIGHT, FOR DIFFERENT THINGS -- reconciled here so the next reader does not have to choose:** * **section 3.6.7** *defines* the Initial Page Write exception and its code: *"occurs when the D bit is 0 even though a UTLB entry contains address translation information matching the virtual address to which a data access (write) is made... Sets exception code H'080 in EXPEVT."* (`sh7750_hardware.txt:9918-9928`) * **section 4.7.4, 'SQ Protection'** *applies* it to the store queues: *"Write type exception judgment is performed for writes to the SQs... a TLB miss exception, protection violation exception, or initial page write exception is generated."* (`:11742-11748`) **The code cites 4.7.4; I cited 3.6.7. Cite BOTH -- 4.7.4 is the one that makes it apply to this window, and 3.6.7 is the one that says what the exception is.** **Ranking, from today's adjudication: 7th of 8.** Latent -- no known guest depends on SQ write-protection. *It is a fidelity gap, not a live corruption, and my earlier 'most severe row in the batch' was severity within that batch, not across the queue.* *** INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-27, and the step that could have KILLED it -- whether SH-4 exempts the store queue from translation -- goes the OTHER WAY. The manual refutes the exemption. (Already documented in-source and filed; today's work is re-verification.) *** **THE BYPASS IS UNCONDITIONAL.** `memory_sh.c:353-357`: ```c /* Store queue region: */ if (vaddr >= 0xe0000000 && vaddr < 0xe4000000) { /* Note/TODO: Take SH4_MMUCR_SQMD into account. */ *return_paddr = vaddr; return 2; } ``` **No `MMUCR.AT` test, no UTLB walk, no PR/D check**, and it returns 2 (read/write). `cpu_sh.c:106` is the only assignment of `translate_v2p`, and the sole SH consumer of `0xe0000000` in `src/cpus/` is `pref_rn` -- **no store instruction special-cases the window**, so every `mov.l Rm,@Rn` into it takes this branch. The preceding arm (`:339-350`) matches neither, so the path is identical with AT=1 and AT=0. *** THE MANUAL SETTLES IT AGAINST THE EXEMPTION, from three directions: *** * **section 4.7.4, SQ Protection** (`sh7750_hardware.txt:11742-11748`): *"When MMU is on -- Operation is in accordance with the address translation information recorded in the UTLB, and MMUCR.SQMD. **Write type exception judgment is performed for writes to the SQs** ... a TLB miss exception, protection violation exception, or **initial page write exception** is generated."* * **section 4.7.3** (`:11691-11696`): *"the ASID, V, SZ, SH, PR, and D bits have the same meaning as for normal address translation."* * **QACR is explicitly the MMU-OFF-only mechanism** (`:11719-11723`, `:10473`), so it is NOT an alternative translation path under AT=1. **AND PRIVILEGE DOES NOT RESCUE IT.** The Data TLB Protection Violation table (`:12632-12640`) gives `PR=00` as **"Only read access possible"** in PRIVILEGED mode, with EXPEVT `0x0A0` read / `0x0C0` write at `:12650`. *** THE ASYMMETRY IS THE CLEANEST STATEMENT OF THE DEFECT: THE READ SIDE IS TRANSLATED AND THE WRITE SIDE IS NOT. *** The flush path at `cpu_sh_instr.c:3706-3765` explicitly checks `SH4_MMUCR_AT` and calls `sh_translate_sq_v2p()` -> `translate_via_mmu()`. The store path does none of it. **WHY THE SHIPPED DETECTOR CANNOT SEE THIS, and it is not a detector defect:** `regress/sh_halt_probe.py:590-599` pins `sq pr00 evt` and `sq d0 evt` to **NOEXC deliberately** -- those rows exercise the read-type PREF path, where no protection or dirty case exists. **No row exercises the STORE side at all**, so the detector is silent here rather than contradicting the finding. **ADJACENT, DISTINCT, ALREADY FILED:** the `SQMD` TODO on that same branch is a SECOND gap -- section 4.7.4 requires an ADDRESS ERROR for a user-mode SQ access when `MMUCR.SQMD = 1` even when translation succeeds, and the store path checks neither. `pref_rn` does check it (`cpu_sh_instr.c:3709-3715`) but raises `EXPEVT_RES_INST` instead -- filed as `sh4sqexpevt`. *** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE and GUEST-REACHABLE. A store into the store-queue window BYPASSES THE MMU, so page protection is not enforced on it. The most severe row in this batch. *** **The mechanism:** the SQ write path does not go through `sh_translate_v2p()` / `translate_via_mmu()` (`memory_sh.c:353-357`, `:203-241`, with the source's own commentary at `:289-303`), so a store into the SQ window lands directly in the device's `sq` array. **Guest access sequence, fully specified by the seat:** 1. guest kernel enables paging (`MMUCR.AT = 1`); 2. guest maps the SQ virtual page `0xe0000000` in the UTLB **valid** (`V=1`) and either **clean** (`D=0`) or **read-only** (`PR=00`); 3. guest issues `mov.l r0, @r1` with `r1 = 0xe0000000`. **Expected on hardware (SH7750 sections 4.7.4 / 3.6.7):** an **Initial Page Write** exception (`EXPEVT = 0x080`) on `D=0`, or a **Data Write Protection** exception on a read-only page. **Actual here:** the store simply succeeds. > **So a guest that maps a page read-only, or clean-for-dirty-tracking, and then stores through the SQ window gets a write that hardware would have faulted.** That is protection and dirty-bit tracking silently not enforced -- not a fidelity nit. **Observable:** the guest `EXPEVT` register after the store -- `0x080` (or the write-protect code) when correct, unchanged when broken. Readable by an ordinary guest load, so no new probe capability is needed. **CHECKABLE AGAINST A PRIMARY SOURCE WE HAVE:** the seat cites SH7750 sections 4.7.4 and 3.6.7, and `_scratchpad/sh7750_hardware.txt` is present and greppable. **Confirm the two sections before the round** -- and read the PROSE, not a figure, per the extraction rule. open

sh4itlbprsh4itlbpr ITLB data array 1 is one bit too wide, and SIX shipped rows now REQUIRE the extra bitsh4itlbpr ITLB data array 1 is one bit too wide, and SIX shipped rows now REQUIRE the extra bit — witness: none -- ASSESSED 2026-08-27 and NOT CHANGED. A rung-3 probe is designable (privileged store/load at 0xf3000000, key on r2 & 0x20) but is deliberately not built: the oracle-correction rule requires re-pinning six SHIPPED rows and measuring the committed build RED *before* any edit, which needs a build the machine embargo forbids. — note: *** FIRST EVIDENCE 2026-08-27, from a farmed codex job. The mask arithmetic is CONFIRMED exactly; the SEVERITY is lower than the seat implied, and the reason is a phrase in the manual the seat did not weigh. *** **CONFIRMED, and recomputed here from the header's own constants rather than transcribed:** `dev_sh4.c:1020-1021` builds the ITLB data-array-1 mask with `SH4_PTEL_PR_MASK` = **0x60, a TWO-bit field**, giving 0x1ffffdfa. Narrowing PR to the ITLB's own `SH4_ITLB_DA1_PR` = 0x40 gives 0x1ffffdda. Both values match the seat digit for digit. **The extra bit is 0x20.** **THE PRIMARY SOURCE AGREES, and it was read as PROSE, not off a figure** (`sh7750_hardware.txt:10035-10036`, section 3.7.2): *"In the data field, PPN is indicated by bits [28:10], V by bit [8], SZ by bits [7] and [4], PR by bit [6], C by bit [3], and SH by bit [1]."* **Bit [6], singular** -- so for the ITLB, bit 5 is not part of PR. The sibling `sh4_utlb_da1` at `:1220-1224` keeps the two-bit mask and is CORRECT: the UTLB's PR really is [6:5]. *** BUT THE SAME FIGURE'S LEGEND (`:10062`) SAYS RESERVED BITS ARE "0 write value, UNDEFINED READ VALUE" -- SO RETURNING 0x20 IS ARCHITECTURALLY PERMITTED, NOT WRONG. *** That single clause is what moves this from 'defect' to 'fidelity nit', and no seat quoted it. **THE SEAT'S LOAD-BEARING PREMISE -- 'no translation decision uses that bit' -- IS TRUE, BUT ONLY VIA A TWO-STEP CHAIN IT DID NOT GIVE, AND I FIRST SCORED IT FALSE.** The single consumer is `memory_sh.c:163`, `pr = (lo & SH4_PTEL_PR_MASK) >> SH4_PTEL_PR_SHIFT` -- a TWO-bit read, and `lo` **can** be `itlb_lo` (`:120-122`). That looks like the bit reaching a decision. It does not, because: 1. `:114-117` -- ITLB entries are walked **only** when `FLAG_INSTR` is set; 2. `:195-200` -- the instruction arm tests **only** `if (!(pr & 2))`, i.e. `pr` bit 1, which is `lo` bit 6, the REAL PR bit. Bit 5 becomes `pr` bit 0, which that arm never reads. The data-side `switch (pr)` at `:206`/`:219` DOES separate 0/1/2/3 -- but the ITLB never reaches it. > **THE LATENT COUPLING, which is the part actually worth carrying:** the bit is inert because of ONE arm's specific test, not because of any structural guarantee. An edit making instruction protection 'more complete' -- replacing `if (!(pr & 2))` with a `switch (pr)` mirroring the data path -- would make a guest-stored reserved bit LIVE, flipping pr=2 into pr=3. Narrowing the store mask would make the inertness structural. *That is the real argument for the change, and it is a defence-in-depth argument, not a correctness one.* **NOT CHANGED, and the cost is why.** Six SHIPPED rows in `#452`'s detector pin the current mask -- R3 and A4i in `sh4_tlbda2_probe.py` (`:37`, `:251`), C1 in `sh4_tlbda2_witness.py` (`:126`) -- all keyed off `ITLB_MASK = ... | _PR | ... # 0x1ffffdfa` (`probe:71`, `witness:53`), which the probe uses as a **per-device signature** (`:68`) to tell ITLB from UTLB. The ADDITION LICENCE wants a measured delta or a transferred warrant; the manual supplies neither, since it makes the present read value legal. And the ORACLE-CORRECTION RULE requires re-pinning those rows FIRST and measuring the committed build RED under the new expectations **before** touching code -- which needs a build. **Correctly queued behind the machine embargo, not skipped.** (The signature property would survive a narrowing: 0x1ffffdda vs the UTLB's 0x1ffffdff still differ.) *Apparatus note, against my own checking rather than the seat's: my first grep for the header constants used `[ ]` in ERE, which is the set {space, backslash, t} and does NOT match a tab -- so it returned NOTHING and I nearly scored the seat unverifiable. Second instance of the same class today, after the `0x3e0` literal-vs-symbol miss on `sh4pcic15`.* open

THE OBSERVABLE ALREADY EXISTS: cpu_sh.c:168-173 registers `iprio_%x` as a readable setting for EVERY 0x20 slot in 0..0xfff, which includes `iprio_3e0` (IRQ15). The hardwired priority loop at cpu_sh.c:390 is `for (i = SH4_INTEVT_IRQ0; i <= SH4_INTEVT_IRQ14; i += 0x20)`, so slot 0x3e0 is never written and keeps 0 while 0x3c0 (IRQ14) gets 1. Two `print` commands on an unmodified machine separate the two. AND RUNG 2 IS THE RIGHT RUNG FOR IT, not a concession: the ladder licenses machine construction as a reproduction for 'defects in code construction itself executes (init-time)', naming the macppc heap OOB #23 as the exemplar. This IS init-time -- the loop populates the priority table at CPU init and the defect is a slot it never reaches. The ladder's warning about rung 2 is that registration proves presence not reachability, for ACCESS-PATH defects; this is not one. WHAT A RUNG-2 WITNESS WOULD NOT SETTLE, said plainly: it observes the priority TABLE, not delivery. It cannot show that an asserted line 15 is dropped -- for that the carrier's free-running shape is required (sr=0x40000000, vbr into RAM, `bra .` after the trigger, breakpoint at VBR+0x600), and driving a PCIC line needs a PCI device landing on line 15, since dev_sh4.c:2951-2967 registers the 16 lines as `<path>.pcic.<i>` for bus_pci_init's pciirq rather than as anything a guest store reaches directly. So the honest split is: the priority-0 STATE is witnessable at rung 2 today; the DROPPED-DELIVERY symptom is not, and the round should not claim it is. STALE CITATION CORRECTED: the row cites dev_sh4.c:2822-2836 for the wiring; that range is now the default arm's fatal()/exit block. The wiring is at :2951-2967.·······

Assessment (initial problem)·✓2026-08-23 — *** WITNESS CONSTRUCTIBLE AT RUNG 3, and the MANUAL confirms the value is wrong. *** dev_sh4.c:2715-2720 is a bare latch -- `odata = d->cpg_frqcr` with no reset value written at init, so a guest reads back whatever DEVINIT's memset left, i.e. 0x0000. THE MANUAL, READ LOCALLY rather than taken from a search summary: _scratchpad/sh7750_hardware.txt:18607-18608 reads 'FRQCR is initialized only by a power-on reset via the RESET pin. The initial value of each bit is determined by the clock operating mode', and the bit table immediately below at :18610-18614 gives initial values CKOEN=1 (bit 11), PLL1EN=1 (bit 10), PLL2EN=1 (bit 9) with bits 15-12 = 0. So the reset value carries at least 0x0E00 and is NEVER 0x0000. The register table at :18476 marks the reset column 'Undefined*'; :18607 is the footnote that explains the asterisk, so 'undefined' means MODE-DEPENDENT, not zero -- a distinction that would have been easy to read the wrong way from the table alone. A guest reading FRQCR therefore sees both PLLs disabled and clock output disabled, the opposite of the reset state. WITNESS: one 16-bit guest load from 0xffc00000 on an unmodified SH-4 machine. HONEST LIMIT, the same shape as sh4pcic15's: the model has no clock-operating-mode concept, so a round must DECIDE what to present rather than read one value off the manual. The three bits above are mode-INDEPENDENT and settle the floor; IFC2 and the divider bits are not.·······

Final review (flagship adjudication)✓2026-08-23 — dev_sh4.c's `case SH4_CPG_FRQCR` models FRQCR as a plain store/load with no initialisation, so a guest reads 0x0000. SH7750 Hardware Manual Rev.7.00 Table 10.3 gives the legal initial values as H'0E1A / H'0E23 / H'0E13 / H'0E0A depending on clock mode. THIS IS THE HONEST LONG-RUN ANSWER TO sh4pclock: real hardware derives the peripheral clock from FRQCR and the mode pins, and a seat measured that the CPU:peripheral ratio in that table is only ever 4 or 6 -- calibrated against dreamcast, whose 200 MHz / 50 MHz = 4 is a legal mode this tree independently knows. A round here could make pclock DERIVED rather than assigned. Note the bound is not enough on its own: machine_hpcsh.c sets no emulated_hz at all, so the tree does not even claim a Jornada CPU clock to divide.········

FILED not fixed: the stopping rule reserves in-round fixes for a MEASURED FALSE PASS or a WRONG RECORD, and #461's detector is above the vacuity floor on all four clauses -- so these are coverage debt, the #447 disposition. *** E1 IS THE FINDING, AND IT DEFEATS THE ROUND'S STRUCTURAL DEFENCE BY GOING ROUND IT. *** Exchange the word- and bit-index expressions in gdrom_unimpl_first (`bits[k >> 5]` / `1u << (k & 31)` transposed). MEASURED, twice, with a standalone probe: four DECLINED 32-bit READS in the CONTROL window write 1 into dma_reg[1] (destination), [2] (length), [3] (count) and [5] (enable) -- which is EXACTLY case 0x18's arming condition, reached from the wrong window entirely. bits is a uint32_t[2]; `bits[k & 31]` runs to index 31 and the struct puts dma_reg[0] six words past it. ASan is blind (member-to-member inside one malloc). *** THE BOUNDS GUARD STILL PASSES: k is still off/4 < nkeys. The round's defence protects the BOUND; E1 lives in the INDEX, and no row was on the index. *** Honest scope from the seat: it is one transposition, and each HALF dies alone (m_swapidx 31/32, m_swapbit 29/32) -- the rows measure key DISTINCTNESS, which a transposition preserves exactly, so the detector catches either half and misses the whole. E2 `|=` -> `=` (32/32): defeats once-per-offset on any REVISIT -- read +0x00, +0x04, +0x00 gives three lines, so a repeated register scan re-floods forever. Every existing row is blind because none revisits a word after touching another in the same bitmap word. E3 the alignment guard rewritten as `len != sizeof(uint32_t)` (32/32): re-opens the alias, MEASURED -- a 4-byte write at DMA+0x05 lands 0xffffffff in dma_reg[1] against the seeded 0x11223344. Every existing guard row uses a NARROW access, so width and alignment are indistinguishable to the detector. No SH4 instruction can issue a misaligned 32-bit store, but memory_rw can, and debugger_cmds.c:1353 is one caller. E4 both alignment ternaries in the DMA diagnostics inverted (32/32) -- the messages lie about dropped-vs-stored and no row reads the text. E5 `if (idata != 0)` -> `if (0)` at case 0x18 (32/32): the DMA arm can be present, correctly routed, and completely INERT. probeslowprobeslow gdrom_default_probe.py's cost is SESSIONS, not rows -- the 1800s overrun was real at 44 rows and is measured false at 52probeslow gdrom_default_probe.py's cost is SESSIONS, not rows -- the 1800s overrun was real at 44 rows and is measured false at 52 — witness: none needed -- a harness cost measurement, not a device defect — note: *** AND THE FEATURE'S VALUE WAS DEMONSTRATED THE SAME HOUR, BY A SEAT THAT BUILT ONE. *** While measuring Round 2's mutants the opus seat wrote its own probe WITH session selection (`tprobe2.py <bin> <img> 'S1 badfmt,S4 acceptA'`) and used it immediately: for the Site A fallthrough mutant it ran TWO sessions instead of eight, because only those two can distinguish a decline from an accept. **That is the argument for the feature and, read carefully, also the argument for why it is a separate round.** Selection is CHEAP in a purpose-built probe where it is designed in; the cost measured here is RETROFITTING it to a 1200-line probe whose 36 sessions run at module level. The two facts are not in tension -- they are the same fact seen from each end, and a future round should read them together rather than citing one. *** A FOURTH COST FACT, MEASURED 2026-08-28, AND IT IS ABOUT THE FIX RATHER THAN THE COST: A ROW FILTER IS NOT A SMALL CHANGE TO THIS PROBE. *** Round 2 was going to fold one in -- the owner approved it on a cost I stated -- and the estimate was wrong by roughly 10x. Measured before building: session() calls at MODULE level (column 0) 36 session() calls inside a block 3 -- 39 **Skipping a row therefore means skipping TOP-LEVEL STATEMENTS.** A filter in `row()` alone changes what is SCORED and saves NOTHING, because the expensive part -- the session -- has already run by the time row() is called. Real per-row selection needs either a label threaded through all 36 call sites with an early-return in session(), or the probe restructured into per-row functions. **WITHDRAWN FROM ROUND 2 BY OWNER DECISION** so the strengthening diff stays about the replacement channel, which is what its pass 2 reviews. It ships as its own round with its own panel and its own negative controls -- a filter that silently selects nothing is this project's most-recorded failure class, and it must not ride in on a diff reviewed for something else. WHEN IT IS BUILT, the guards are already specified: print a DENOMINATOR (`selected N of 58`) beside every result; HARD-FAIL on zero matches; HARD-FAIL on a selector naming a row that does not exist (so a renamed row cannot silently stop being tested); and unset MUST be byte-identical to today, which is the negative control the gate itself provides. Name derived from the tree rather than invented: `GDROM_DEF_ROWS` -- the house idiom is `os.environ.get("<TOOL>_<KNOB>")` (SELFMUTANT_RUN_TIMEOUT and friends) and this probe already owns the GDROM_DEF_ namespace via GDROM_DEF_RESULT= / GDROM_DEF_VECTOR=. *** AND THE GATE PINS THE DENOMINATOR AT 58: *** gate_sh_rounding.sh names rows in a `for v in ...` list and checks the ratio, so any filter must leave the unset-path denominator untouched. *** A THIRD COST VARIABLE, MEASURED 2026-08-27: COMMANDS PER SESSION. *** This row's headline is *"cost is SESSIONS, not rows"*, and that was derived from probes whose rows each run one short session. **A row added to `asic_badaddr_probe.py` today is ONE session -- cheap by this row's own measure -- and took roughly SIX MINUTES.** ``` the other 13 rows ~15 s each one session, a handful of debugger commands `sweep 256` ~6 min one session, 768 debugger commands ``` It walks all 256 offsets of the SYSASIC window with `r1=<addr>; pc=<code>; step 1` per offset. Each of those is a pty round-trip, and the round-trips dominate: the emulator work itself is 256 byte loads. **SO THE RULE NEEDS A SECOND TERM.** A probe's wall clock is roughly `sessions x boot_cost + total_debugger_commands x round_trip`, and the two terms are traded against each other by DESIGN CHOICES that look unrelated: folding N rows into one session removes N boots and keeps every command. **THE CHEAPER SHAPE, not built:** drive the walk from GUEST CODE -- a loop, or an unrolled block written once with `put h` -- so one `step N` replaces hundreds of round-trips. Not done today because hand-assembling SH is this project's documented encoding trap, and a wrong encoding yields a probe that measures the wrong thing while looking green. *Recorded rather than acted on: the six minutes buys a row that defends 256 offsets where nine were defended before, and the alternative risks a silently-wrong instrument.* open

That loop exits only when bit 3 is SET and bit 7 CLEAR; +0x18's domain is {0 idle, 1 busy} and neither ANDs to 0x08 -- IT WOULD HANG ON CORRECT HARDWARE. Independently, dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:722-737 -- code this round never touched -- documents that same wait as NetBSD's COMMAND-START handshake on the CONTROL window's BUSY register and sets d->busy |= 0x08 in reply. The exhibit was lifted from that comment and re-pointed at a register it says nothing about. The conclusion survives on Linux; the reason does not, and a wrong reason gets reused -- this project already has the fatal()-is-byte-for-byte-debug() case on record. All four corrected IN PLACE. This is the #357/#362/#365 shape: citations from panel output rather than a local source. It is NOT vestigial (a `diff_*.c` was touched on 2026-08-21, #449) but it is no longer where the detectors live: the last probe edit was 2026-08-23, #461. *** THE DEFECT IS THE MESSAGE, NOT THE SELECTOR. *** `no detector added or modified` is TRUE of `diff_*.c` and FALSE of the commit, and a reader has no way to tell which was meant -- the same shape as a pattern that matched nothing reporting zero for everything, and the same shape as the freshly-rejected section X, which printed `every cited measurement exists` while checking 2 of 8. The two sub-checks port directly -- the IDENTITY guard has a probe analogue (a row asserting its own row count, which gate_sh_rounding.sh already pins per probe) and the MUTATION-RUN soft reminder is if anything more apt for a probe, since probe kill tables are where this project's mutation work actually happens. **DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED IN #462:** widening it would change a gate's behaviour while that gate's own subject is under a 15-run measurement, and this round has spent the day learning why that ordering matters.open

Exactly the three-membered-option-set rule, biting the ruling that invoked it. *** THE ADDITION LICENCE NOW CLEARS ON A MEASURED DELTA, which it did not before: *** V0 compiles the feared edit, V3 refuses it, and **all 21 real events keep BYTE-IDENTICAL addresses**. That is the A-vs-B measurement the licence asks for, and it is why this ships rather than staying a comment. It also mispaired `96..127 -> +0x0c, +0x1c`, which is the same band-to-address error the device file had already corrected an earlier draft for. Restated STRUCTURALLY: the macro treats the event's high bits as a word index into the whole 64-word register file, when only words 0-2 are the `pending_irq` group. *And a clobber is worse than the comment implied: the mask cases carry no hack-bit discrimination and the store is a wholesale replacement with the tick called immediately, so the raise both FAILS and DESTROYS the guest's programmed IRQ mask.* *** THREE APPARATUS FAILURES OF MINE ON THE WAY, ALL DOCUMENTED CLASSES, RECORDED BECAUSE THE THIRD IS NEW: *** 1. my verification harness redefined `SYSASIC_BASE`, which the header owns -- every leg died of `redefined` and the feared-edit leg's 'pass' was a **FALSE PASS**, failing for the wrong reason. Rule 4 caught it: *did it fail for the reason under test?* 2. I wrote the guard with a Python string instead of `chr(92)` and put a **literal ` ` into product code** where a line continuation belongs -- the documented Bash->heredoc->Python trap, propagated to all four trees before I caught it. 3. **NEW, AND WORTH THE SPACE: my own comment's worked example -- `#define SYSASIC_EVENT_FOO 96` -- POISONED THE CENSUS that greps the header for event defines.** The harness read the DOCUMENTATION as SOURCE and built a program out of the very construct the comment forbids. **A comment containing an example of a forbidden construct breaks any census that greps for that construct.** Same shape as the grep that matched a comment and was read as code earlier the same day. *** ADJUDICATED 2026-08-26. MY DISSOLUTION READING HELD -- AND MY FOLD WAS HALF WRONG, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. *** **THE DISSOLUTION CONFIRMED, MEASURED:** every event raise is a `memory_rw` write through the device decode. `SYSASIC_TRIGGER_EVENT` computes the address and issues the write; `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR` has exactly TWO occurrences in `src/` -- its definition and that one use -- and every in-tree raiser goes through the macro. The arrays are declared file-locally in the `.c`, so no other unit can index them. **There is no bypass, so the vendored-header LICENCE QUESTION IS MOOT** -- the guard need never live in the header. *** BUT THE HEADER DEFECT IS BROADER THAN THE r==3 INVARIANT, AND THE EXCESS IS EXACTLY WHAT AN r-GUARD CANNOT SEE. Verified here by arithmetic and by reading the case: *** e=96..127 -> +0x0c r=3 default: -- DROPPED (an r-guard covers this) e=128..159 -> +0x10 r=0 *** case 0x10: `d->mask_13[r] = idata` -- LEGAL WRITE *** e=256..287 -> +0x20 r=0 *** case 0x20: another legal mask case *** e>=2048 -> +0x100+ OUTSIDE the device window entirely **A raise in [128,159] is decoded as a perfectly legal mask write and CLOBBERS a mask register the guest programmed.** Memory-safe, guest-visible, and invisible to any guard on `r` -- because r is 0, not 3. So the row FOLDS ONLY HALFWAY: the fourth-word half is covered by `asicindexcase`'s already-adjudicated #463b decline at zero added cost; **this row survives as DOCUMENT-ONLY for the mask-clobber bands and the window escape.** **THE TRUE STATEMENT OF THE DEFECT: `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR` is correct only for e in [0,95].** The old title said it 'routes any event >= 96 to relative 0x0c' -- FALSE, true only of [96,127] -- and it contradicted this row's own tail correction AND the shipped comment in the device file, which already says *'an earlier draft said any event >= 96, which is false'*. **The queue's most-read field carried a falsehood its own body had corrected.** Title rewritten. *** AND I REPEATED THAT SAME FALSE UNIVERSAL TO THE ADJUDICATOR while asking the question -- 'Every event >= 96 gives (e)>>5 == 3' -- when the correction already existed in TWO of my own shipped records. *** A brief built on my own uncorrected summary rather than on my own corrected record: the dropped-qualifier class, aimed at the seat I was asking for help. **THE COMPILE-TIME ASSERT IS REJECTED ON SHAPE, NOT ON LICENCE, and the reason is this project's own named class.** An assert can only reference NAMED terms, so it pins today's max (`67>>5 == 2`, already true) while a future `#define SYSASIC_EVENT_FOO 96` -- **the exact feared edit** -- adds a name the assert does not mention and compiles clean. **A check that cannot fail on its own target mutant.** The `SH4_VAL` enum idiom does not transfer either: sparse hardware numbers need explicit `= n` per member and a terminal count sees only members above it. **The house precedent points the other way and is in this very device family**: `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` chose *'Stated rather than asserted: `_Static_assert` is C11 and this tree is C99'*. Follow it -- STATE the domain restriction. CLOSING ARTIFACT: a 2-5 line comment in the header beside the macro -- the one place a future event-adder's eyes are guaranteed to be -- pointing at the device file's existing #463 invariant comment, which already points back. A comment adds no product code, so the addition licence is not even triggered. Tag it `/* #NNN: */` per house ethos. Must land byte-identical in `est/`. *Premises the adjudicator discharged: the two-commit thirdparty figure CONFIRMED -- and sharper than I had it, since `8dd86b5` touched four thirdparty headers but NOT this one, so **this fork has never edited it**; the `[3]` arrays CONFIRMED; and 'a device-file comment cannot govern a header #define' is TRUE of the comment and HALF-TRUE of the guard, which is exactly why the row folds halfway.* *** THE THREE ASIC ROWS REST ON ONE INVARIANT, AND TWO OF THEM MAY BE ONE FIX. Scoped 2026-08-26 by reading, no run. *** **THE SHARED INVARIANT: `r == 3` is unreachable by any implemented case.** VERIFIED by reading the switch labels -- they are three CONSECUTIVE words at group bases `0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30`, so `r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3` yields 0, 1, 2 and never 3. All three rows are that one invariant, differing only in **which edit would break it**: asiceventaddr a #define in the vendored HEADER (event >= 96 -> offset 0x0c) asicindexcase an indexing `case` added at an r==3 offset in the DEVICE FILE asicoffsetkill an adversarial MUTANT at an r==3 offset no detector row touches **THE THIRD IS DIFFERENT IN KIND and should not be folded with the other two:** it is a DETECTOR-COVERAGE question, not a product invariant. `kill far` (+0xfc) was added to defeat a GROUP-NARROWING mutant and cannot defeat a SINGLE-OFFSET one; the seat that raised it said plainly it did not build it. *** THE FINDING THAT MAY FOLD THE OTHER TWO, and it contradicts `asiceventaddr`'s own stated reason for being a separate row: *** that row argues a device-file comment "cannot govern a `#define` added to a header". **True of a COMMENT. Not true of a GUARD.** An event `>= 96` does not stay in the header -- it becomes an ADDRESS the driver accesses, arriving at the device as `relative_addr == 0x0c` and decoding to `r == 3`. **So a guard on `r` in the device file would catch the header entry point too**, because the header case MANIFESTS as a device-file access. If that holds, one guard covers both rows and the vendored-header edit -- the expensive part, on a file this fork has touched once -- may be unnecessary. **Stated as a question rather than a conclusion because I have not built it**, and the adjudicator was asked the licence question on the header assumption; this finding is being sent to it as a correction rather than acted on unilaterally. STOP CONDITION: if the guard-covers-both reading holds, fold `asiceventaddr` into `asicindexcase` as one fix with two entry points and close it as a duplicate; if it does not, the rows stay separate and the header licence question stands. *** SCOPED 2026-08-26 WITHOUT A RUN -- the row is read-only by construction, and the scoping found a CONSTRAINT that changes the fix's cost. *** **THE FIX SITE IS A VENDORED THIRDPARTY HEADER.** The macro is at `src/include/thirdparty/dreamcast_sysasicvar.h`, which carries BOTH a GXemul `$Id$` and an upstream **`$NetBSD: sysasicvar.h,v 1.5`** line. **MEASURED: `git log --all -- 'src/include/thirdparty/*'` returns TWO commits -- the 0.7.0 import, and the single ~119-correction hardening commit.** So this fork has edited thirdparty exactly ONCE. *The precedent is not absent, and it cuts both ways: the header's own banner says it was "Extended with useful macros and also some more event definitions described in KOS comments", so GXemul UPSTREAM already extends this vendored file. Editing it is precedented -- it is just rare, and rarity is the cost.* **WHY THAT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TRIVIA:** the row's whole reason for existing separately is that *the edit which reaches this defect adds a `#define` to a header, with no device-file change at all* -- so a structural-invariant comment in `dev_dreamcast_asic.c` cannot govern it. **The only place a guard can sit is the same rarely-touched header**, which means the fix's licence question is sharper than for an in-file addition. **THE CANDIDATE FIX, stated so it can be adjudicated rather than argued:** a compile-time assertion beside the macro, so that adding an event `>= 96` fails the BUILD rather than silently routing to relative `0x0c` and indexing three-element arrays at 3. It is self-verifying by construction -- a negative control is one test `#define` -- and it costs nothing at runtime. **BUT IT IS AN ADDITION TO PRODUCT CODE, so the ADDITION LICENCE governs: a MEASURED DELTA or a TRANSFERRED WARRANT, never 'it cannot hurt'.** The delta cannot be measured without a build, and the machine is reserved (owner directive 2026-08-26: hold off on anything needing an idle machine). **`asicbadaddr` is the natural warrant donor** -- same device, same `r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3` decode, same three-element arrays -- and whether that transfers to a THIRDPARTY header edit is exactly the judgement an adjudicator owes rather than me. *** WHAT IS NOT IN DOUBT AND NEEDED NO RUN: the arithmetic. *** `(e)>>5 == 3` for every `e >= 96`; the highest defined event is 67; therefore latent today, and reachable by a one-line header addition by anyone adding a high event number. Two seats confirmed both numbers from source on 2026-08-24 and I re-derived the macro form here. NEXT ACTION: adjudicate the licence and the thirdparty-edit question. NOT shipped unilaterally -- a rarely-touched vendored header is precisely where 'it cannot hurt' does the most damage. RAISED BY THE opus5 SEAT on the asicbadaddr pass-1 panel (panel_20260824_231824), ADJUDICATED 2026-08-24. `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR(e)` is `SYSASIC_BASE + 4*((e)>>5)`, so ANY event number >= 96 gives `(e)>>5 == 3` and a relative offset of 0x0c -- which `dev_dreamcast_asic.c`'s `r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3` maps to index 3 of three-element arrays. **LATENT AND PROVABLY SO: the highest defined event is 67 (MATOUTOFMEM), and both the 67 and the 96 threshold were confirmed from source by two seats.** *** WHY IT IS A SEPARATE ROW RATHER THAN PART OF asicbadaddr: THE EDIT THAT REACHES IT ADDS A #define TO A HEADER, WITH NO CHANGE TO THE DEVICE FILE AT ALL -- so the structural-invariant comment asicbadaddr plans to leave in `dev_dreamcast_asic.c` CANNOT GOVERN IT. *** Post-fix the failure mode also changes rather than disappearing: an event >= 96 would write to 0x0c, fall to `default:`, and the pending bit would be SILENTLY LOST where pre-fix it was `exit(1)`. Neither is correct; neither is reachable today. *** DISPOSITION: NO RUNTIME GUARD *** -- a guard that cannot fire is the insurance-that-isn't this tree already rejects. The carrier is a one-line comment at the event-define block IN THE HEADER. **FILED RATHER THAN SHIPPED THIS ROUND, and the reason is the file class:** the header lives under `src/include/thirdparty/`, which this fork HAS edited (the 8dd86b5 hardening commit) but where NO file carries the `/* #NNN: */ ` correction tag the ethos otherwise requires -- so the convention for editing it is unsettled, and settling it is not this round's job. *** THE MANDATORY HALF IS THE RECORD, NOT THE COMMENT: `asicbadaddr` must SCOPE its invariant claim to `dev_dreamcast_asic.c` and name this header path as a separate latent item, rather than claiming the invariant is fully protected. *** *** CORRECTED 2026-08-25 BY THE #463 RECORDS AUDIT (`_scratchpad/panel_20260825_024101_audit`, grok seat), and the correction makes this row STRONGER. *** Every earlier statement of this row said the macro reaches `0x0c` for "any event >= 96". **That is false**: `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR(e) = SYSASIC_BASE + 4*((e)>>5)` (`dreamcast_sysasicvar.h:74`) sends `e` in `[128,159]` to `+0x10`, which is r = 0 and perfectly legal. The true predicate is `(e>>5) & 3 == 3` -- `[96,127]` -> `+0x0c`, `[224,255]` -> `+0x1c`, `[352,383]` -> `+0x2c`, `[480,511]` -> `+0x3c`. So the violator is not a single range above a threshold but a REPEATING FAMILY that lands on the fourth word of every 16-byte group -- the same structural shape as `asicbadaddr` itself, one level up in the header. Verified by enumerating `4*(e>>5)` over `e>>5` in `[0,15]`. The LATENCY argument is unchanged and still holds: max over all 21 `SYSASIC_EVENT_*` defines is 67 (`:72`), and `67>>5 == 2` lands at `+0x08`.open

THE ROW BUDGET, and it is bounded ON PRINCIPLE rather than by restraint: (1) **UPGRADE the four r==3 rows' oracle** to assert the returned value is the defined 0. They are survive-only today; they already READ, so this only adds the assertion. This discharges an adjudicator condition open since the FIRST adjudication ('confirm the kill rows check the decline VALUE, not survival alone'), never discharged, and now load-bearing because the candidates differ exactly in decline-column semantics. (2) **ONE BOUND ROW**: the fix now ADDS a predicate (`n < 8`), so clause (d) / accept-failability owes a row that reddens when the bound is REMOVED -- count <= 8 occurrences across the probe's 64 r==3 accesses. **Pin the COUNT, not the message text.** (3) One contract sentence. EXPECTED EQUIVALENCE, recorded in advance so it is not mistaken for an escape: the decline-nulled mutant (`if (r == 3)` kept, fall-through restored) will likely measure EQUIVALENT at base, because `default:` declines identically -- the #449 pattern, an equivalence RESULT and not a failure. MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE: base is an INVARIANCE CONTROL, never a discriminator -- all candidates are guest-identical at base and a detector should pin CONTRACT, not implementation. The evidence is entirely in the mutant deltas, and the translation mutants must go STRICTLY REDDER (`+1` -> safe 8, `+2` -> safe 4, `-1` -> asic ok; arithmetic verified). **Base must be RE-RUN on the latched build, not inherited** -- 8 new `fatal()` lines enter the pty logs, and `gate_hygiene` GRADES pty logs, which is a known trap class here: a new diagnostic entering graded logs must be shown green, not assumed. CLOSE-OUT: full 13-mutant table on the latched build, pass 2 on the real diff, targeted gate, one commit, and then #463 and #463b are OVER -- the next dissent on this device buys a new round or a filed row, never a reopening. *** FINAL FORM 2026-08-25: A SILENT FALL-THROUGH DECLINE. THE LATCH IS DEAD. *** `if (r == 3) { /* comment */ } else switch (...)` -- a guarded arm joining the EXISTING epilogue, NOT an early return. That form uses the tail's own `memory_writemax64` so nothing is duplicated, and it does not lean on the dispatcher pre-zeroing read buffers (`memory_rw.c:485`) -- codex's objection answered STRUCTURALLY rather than by trusting a non-local guarantee. *** WHY THE LATCH DIED, on two independent closures either of which is fatal. *** (1) THE PREDICATE IS EMPTY WHERE IT MATTERS: implemented registers occupy words 0-2 of all four groups (documentarily grounded -- Linux mach-dreamcast and KallistiOS both show three words per group, no fourth), so every r==3 lane in modelled space sits directly above an implemented word-2 register and IS the second lane of a legal 8-byte access. 'Latch only on offsets that are not a lane of a legal multi-word access' selects the EMPTY SET -- a dead guard, and this round has refused three of those already. (2) THE INFORMATION IS ABSENT, NOT MERELY AWKWARD: the decoder issues two independent 32-bit accesses, so at the handler **the second half of a legal fmov.d and a direct probe of a reserved word are BYTE-IDENTICAL CALLS.** No predicate written inside this function separates them at any complexity. A dispatcher-layer latch, where transaction context exists, is a different change to a different file -- out of scope. *** AND IT REWRITES THIS ROUND'S FINDING 5: the deleted `fatal()` did not merely print unconditionally, it printed ON LEGAL TRAFFIC -- the second half of every 8-byte access to an implemented register. The 'self-announcing property' the latch was meant to restore was PARTLY A FALSE-ALARM PROPERTY ALL ALONG, so the trade the deletion made was SMALLER than finding 5 claimed and smaller than the latch ruling claimed on top of it. *** THE COMMENT MUST CARRY THE INOCULATION, one line: *silent by design -- r==3 lanes occur inside legitimate split accesses (fmov.d, SQ), so any diagnostic here false-alarms.* That sentence is what stops the next reader re-deriving the latch. WARRANT, THREE INDEPENDENT LEGS: the measured anchor (`+1`->safe 8, `+2`->safe 4 closing the one mutant that escaped everything, `-1`->asic ok); enforcement by control flow instead of enumeration; and the UB upgrade -- a broken invariant buys UNDEFINED BEHAVIOUR a compiler may exploit, not a defined overlap, which makes the decline the only C-meaningful statement of the bound in executable form. DETECTOR DELTA: **the bound-count row DIES WITH THE LATCH** -- it was the latch's own accept-failability obligation, and no predicate means no row. The r==3 value upgrade stays.open

asicarray4asicarray4 sizing the ASIC's four register arrays [4] instead of [3] would de-fang the whole out-of-bounds classasicarray4 sizing the ASIC's four register arrays [4] instead of [3] would de-fang the whole out-of-bounds class — witness: none -- design proposal, not a defect — note: RAISED BY THE kimi SEAT on the #463 pass-2 panel (_scratchpad/panel_20260825_020219), via `kimi-k3:cloud` because the kimi CLI is quota-walled -- a DIFFERENT TRANSPORT, recorded as a substitute. The struct declares `pending_irq[3]`, `mask_13[3]`, `mask_11[3]`, `mask_9[3]` consecutively, so `mask_13[4]` IS `mask_11[1]` and any mask widening corrupts a neighbour silently. Padding each to [4] converts that class from CORRUPTION back to mere silent wrongness at a cost of 16 bytes. **The seat was explicit that this is a TRADE, not a fix**, and that framing is the reason to keep it: it does not make a wrong index right, it only stops it reaching another array. Weigh against `asicindexcase`, which it would also partly de-fang. *** MEASURED AND PARTLY REFUTED 2026-08-25 by the opus5 research seat, which had first FAVOURED this option and then argued against it. *** Sizing the arrays [4] makes the `+1` translation mutant **ESCAPE** `mask9 rt`. The row's kill mechanism is that DEVICE_TICK ERASES `asserted_13` (`d->asserted_13 = ... = 0`, loop bound i<3) and the mask_9 write arm calls the tick immediately -- so at [3] the stored 0xb2 lands on asserted_13, is wiped, and the readback reddens the row. **At [4], index 3 is a real slot the tick never touches, the value survives, and the mutant escapes**: N=3 readback 0x0 (RED, killed) vs N=4 readback 0xb2 (GREEN, ESCAPES). So this option **costs a mutant kill and needs a replacement row before it can ship** -- the original filing ("de-fangs the whole OOB class for 16 bytes") understated its cost and is corrected here. Filing it rather than shipping it was right for a reason the filing did not know. *** DEAD BY THREE INDEPENDENT ROUTES, which is the strongest refutation this round produced for any alternative. *** (i) agy's phantom-state argument -- it invents hardware that does not exist and leaves the tick loop ignoring the fourth word; (ii) opus5's MEASUREMENT -- it makes the `+1` mutant ESCAPE `mask9 rt`, because that row's kill works by the tick erasing the cell and [4] gives index 3 a real slot the tick never touches; (iii) codex's HARDWARE ORACLE -- Linux's mach-dreamcast IRQ code documents three status words and three per mask group, and KallistiOS exposes exactly +0/+4/+8 with no fourth. **The three-word bound is a HARDWARE FACT, not an implementation choice.** Three seats, three methods, one conclusion -- and note this round holds NO Holly ASIC documentation of its own, so route (iii) is the first external oracle it ever obtained.open

seatthinkburnseatthinkburn a FIFTH seat-failure class: an empty response wrapped in 260 KB of thinking, which every size check scores as the panel's best answerseatthinkburn a FIFTH seat-failure class: an empty response wrapped in 260 KB of thinking, which every size check scores as the panel's best answer — commits: a4d054d — witness: measured -- _scratchpad/panel_20260825_024101_audit/consistency_deepseek-v4-pro_cloud.txt — note: *** TWO MORE INSTANCES 2026-08-26, BACK TO BACK, AND THEY CARRY A CORRELATION THIS ROW DID NOT HAVE: THE BURN TRACKS BRIEF COMPLEXITY, NOT THE SEAT. *** panel_20260826_090604 4,032 b normal answer panel_20260826_190055 2,845 b normal answer panel_20260826_222557 142,525 b BURNED done_reason=length eval_count=65536 panel_20260826_230207 222,981 b BURNED done_reason=length eval_count=65536 **The two burns are on the day's two most COMPLEX briefs** -- one asking it to verify band arithmetic across three separate claims, one asking five questions spanning two rounds. The two clean runs were simpler briefs to the same seat, same transport, same day. *** THAT REFRAMES THE CLASS. *** The row recorded it as a SEAT property -- something to detect and work around. Today's evidence says it is at least partly a BRIEF property, which is actionable in a way a seat outage is not: **I can shorten the brief.** That matches the carrier's oldest lesson about packet-fed seats -- their behaviour is governed by the brief, and this project once spent DAYS misdiagnosing a brief defect as a seat outage. **AND THE SECOND BURN SHOWS WHAT IS BEING LOST, which the first instance could not.** Its output ends mid-sentence: *'So verdict likely NOT RATIFY due to #467. But maybe the question is from a panel'* -- **it had REACHED a verdict and was second-guessing itself when the budget ran out.** That is a substantive dissent destroyed by a token limit, not a seat with nothing to say. On that same panel the other dissenting seat found a LIVE DEFECT, so a lost dissent here is not hypothetical cost. **DETECTION IS ALREADY SOLVED AND SHOULD NOT BE RE-ARGUED:** `seat_verdicts.py` reports these as `SEAT DOWN -- spent its whole budget on hidden reasoning (length, N tokens)`, by reading `done_reason` rather than size. Both of today's burns were caught and named correctly. **WHAT IS STILL OWED is the MITIGATION, and it is now cheap to state:** keep a packet-fed brief to ONE question with the facts inlined, rather than a multi-part audit. Splitting a complex brief across two firings costs one extra invocation and preserves the answer. MEASURED 2026-08-25 on the #463 consistency audit. `deepseek-v4-pro:cloud` returned **`"response": ""` -- completely empty -- inside a 265,845-byte JSON object whose `thinking` field is 260,678 bytes, with `done_reason: 'length'` and `eval_count: 65536`. It spent its ENTIRE output budget on hidden reasoning and never emitted an answer. *** IT IS DISTINCT FROM ALL FOUR RECORDED CLASSES. *** Not a WALL (no quota text, no 403/429). Not the ECHO-ONLY shape (it echoes nothing). Not a REFUSED CONNECTION (the daemon served it fine, for 267 seconds). Not the shared-transport outage (the other three cloud seats answered normally in the same firing). *** AND IT DEFEATS EVERY SIZE-BASED CHECK IN THE WORST DIRECTION: at 265 KB it is the LARGEST file in its panel and would be scored the best answer. *** The carrier already warns 'verify the CONTENT, never the size; the failure mode is a big file' -- this is that lesson in a new variant, where the bulk is not an echoed brief but the model's own reasoning. **It was diagnosable only by accident**: `panel_ollama.py` does `body = resp.get('response') or json.dumps(resp)`, so an empty response falls back to dumping the raw JSON. Had it written the empty string, the file would have been 0 bytes and indistinguishable from a transport failure. That fallback should be made deliberate, and documented as the thing that preserves the diagnosis. THE FIX, and it is cheap: the seat check must parse any Ollama output that starts with `{`, and report SEAT DOWN when `response` is empty -- naming `done_reason` and `eval_count`, because `length` says 'budget exhausted' while `stop` would say something else entirely. A working checker exists (used to produce this row) and needs wiring into `panel.sh` and `seat_verdicts.py`. CONTRIBUTING CAUSE worth recording separately: the brief was the ENTIRE 18 KB round-block draft. The carrier's rule is to INLINE every fact for packet-fed seats, and that rule is sound -- but inlining an 18 KB artifact and asking for exhaustive cross-checking gives a thinking model enough to reason itself past its own budget. **Inline the facts; do not inline an entire document and ask for an audit of it.** *** AND A SIXTH CLASS, MEASURED THE SAME SESSION on the matrix-review panel: THE SEAT'S OWN TRANSPORT DIED MID-ANSWER. *** `agy` returned 293 bytes reading `I have launched the topic cluster analysis script ... Waiting for background script completion.` followed by `Error: the connection to the agent was interrupted before the response finished: subscriber fell behind updates, stalled for 6s`. It is none of the five: no quota text (not a wall), it connected and worked for minutes (not a refused connection), it echoed nothing, it emitted a real partial answer rather than an empty response inside vast thinking, and the other seats on the same panel were unaffected (not the shared-Agent-tool outage). **The distinguishing shape: the seat DELEGATED to a background script and its own streaming connection dropped while it waited.** Two consequences. (1) The keyword set every seat check in this project uses -- quota / rate limit / balance / 403 / 429 / refused -- does NOT contain `interrupted`, `stalled`, or `subscriber fell behind`, so this scored as `answered`. Widened. (2) **It is worth RE-FIRING, unlike a wall**: a wall is the provider refusing and you wait it out; this is a dropped connection and the work simply did not survive. The re-fire rule the carrier already states for walled seats applies here with better odds. *** THE CONTRIBUTING CAUSE THIS ROW FILED WAS MEASURED FALSE THE SAME SESSION. *** It said the trigger was inlining an entire 18 KB document and asking for an exhaustive audit of it, and prescribed 'inline the facts; do not inline a document'. **A SECOND burn then happened on a brief a fraction of that size** -- 11 ledger rows, truncated narratives, ~10 KB -- with the identical signature: `response: ""`, `done_reason: 'length'`, `eval_count: 65536`, and 275,778 bytes of `thinking`. Larger thinking than the first burn, on a much smaller brief. **So SIZE IS NOT THE CAUSE**, and the prescription derived from it was wrong. What the two share is the TASK SHAPE, not the input size: both asked for an EXHAUSTIVE PER-ITEM AUDIT with several independent sub-questions per item (four categories over a document; four questions over each of eleven rows). The seat answered a 6.5 KB pass-2 REVIEW brief normally in the same session -- one subject, one set of questions. **The working hypothesis is now COMBINATORIAL: N items x M orthogonal questions, where the seat appears to explore the cross-product before emitting anything.** That is a hypothesis, not a measurement, and it is recorded as such -- the honest state is that the cause is NOT ESTABLISHED and the first stated cause is REFUTED. OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, which does not depend on the cause: **deepseek is unreliable for per-item audit tasks and reliable for single-subject review**, so route it accordingly rather than by brief size. And the detection rule is unchanged and now doubly warranted: parse the JSON, report SEAT DOWN on an empty `response`, and never score by file size -- both burns produced the LARGEST file in their panel. *** AND THE TEST THAT LOOKED LIKE A CONFIRMATION IS CONFOUNDED -- CORRECTED IMMEDIATELY RATHER THAN LEFT STANDING. *** deepseek ANSWERED a #463 research-stage brief cleanly (1,724 bytes, a real dissent) after burning on two audits, and that was momentarily reported as confirming the task-shape hypothesis over the size hypothesis. **It confirms nothing.** The brief was 3,614 bytes -- SMALLER than both that burned it (19,395 and 10,408) -- so it varies BOTH suspected causes at once and cannot discriminate between them. The honest state of the evidence: burns at 19,395 (per-item audit) and 10,408 (per-item audit); clean answers at 8,583 (single-subject review) and 3,614 (single-subject research). **Size and shape are perfectly correlated across all four data points**, so nothing here separates them. A discriminating test exists and is cheap -- a LARGE single-subject brief, or a SMALL per-item one -- and until someone runs it the cause remains NOT ESTABLISHED. *Recorded because the first stated cause was already refuted once; a second unearned cause would be the same defect with better manners.*open

ALSO REFUTED HERE, and worth keeping because it was checkable in two minutes: the claim that `fbwitness` is ALONE among its 2026-08-20 cohort in being closed. That cohort is 84 rows -- 17 closed, 43 held, 11 dropped, 13 in work -- and four of the closed share `fbwitness`'s exact closure string. A seat's argument from 'this row is the only one' is worth checking every time; this one was wrong. *** FIVE SEATS, ELEVEN ROWS, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS THE EVIDENCE RATHER THAN THE NOISE. *** agy, kimi-k3, glm-5.2, minimax-m3 and grok each assigned a correct state to all eleven rows, reading the same ledger under the same four validity rules stated in the brief. **They agree on only 4 of 11.** `hpcshcpu` drew THREE different answers (closed / dropped / held); six more drew two. This is what a field with no derivable meaning looks like from the outside: competent independent readers do not converge, because there is nothing to converge ON. *** IT ALSO PARTITIONS THE ROUND CLEANLY, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART. *** **UNANIMOUS (4) -- and all four are ALREADY IN THE RIGHT STATE**: `gdromdmadefault` and `witnessinvisible` (closed, missing `commits`), `m437ord` (closed, missing `closure.by`), `cmtattr` (held, correct as-is). What these need is FIELDS, not state changes, and a field that is absent is absent under any definition of `state` -- so they are repairable NOW, independently of the rule question. **SPLIT (7)**: rtcdet, fbwitness, gdromdmawidth, gate3scope, m8invpred, ledgerwitness, hpcshcpu. Every one of these turns on what `state` MEANS, and none can be repaired until that is settled -- editing them now would be manufacturing the appearance of correctness by picking whichever seat I found most persuasive. **THE SPLIT IS ALSO A CHECK ON THE 23-ROW FINDING**, arrived at from the opposite direction: that one measured one closure string against three states; this one measures five readers against one row set. Both say the same thing and neither depends on the other's method. *** ADJUDICATED 2026-08-25, AND IT REFRAMED THE ROUND WHILE CONVICTING ME OF ONE OVERREACH. *** The ruling: `state` and `closure.note` are different TENSES. The note is a PAST-TENSE event log of what happened to a STAGE; `state` is a PRESENT-TENSE assertion of what the ROW still OWES. **Under that reading the multi-state spread of one closure string is the ledger WORKING AS DESIGNED, not the defect** -- rows that experienced the same stage event legitimately differ in what else they owe -- and the stage-coverage test failing is CORROBORATION rather than a second mystery, because state depends on what REMAINS, not on how much happened. **SO THE THING TO FILE IS THE MISSING SCHEMA SEMANTICS, NOT THE SPREAD.** That single absence is the cause behind six mis-counts in one session, two seats inferring opposite conventions from one string, and five seats agreeing on only 4 of 11 rows. The fix is written: a `state_semantics` block now sits in the ledger's own schema, PENDING OWNER RATIFICATION, forward-only in the same way `witness` was. *** MY OVERREACH, RETRACTED IN PLACE: I wrote that 'for most of the 11 there is no fact of the matter to restore -- only a decision'. THAT IS FALSE AND IT WAS CONVENIENT FOR ME*** -- it converts eleven tedious substance reads into one interesting rule question. What died was a repair METHOD (derive state from the note), not the fact of the matter, which is read from commits, gates, holds and filed questions -- exactly how `asicbadaddr` was closed, with no note convention needed. **The seminar is over in one paragraph; the eleven reads remain owed.** *** AND NO NUMBER IN THIS ROW MAY BE QUOTED AS A PREMISE UNTIL A SECOND PARTY CHECKS IT. *** I have mis-counted this ledger six times in one session. Every ruling above depends on the EXISTENCE of the spread, not its size -- ONE held row and ONE closed row sharing a closure string already prove non-derivability -- so the whole second-party check is two greps. The figures 23, 84 and the 1.8/1.8/1.9 stage means are UNVERIFIED SUPPORTING COLOUR, labelled as such, and are leads rather than premises. *** A SEVENTH COUNTING HAZARD, FOUND BY MAKING IT: SEAT NAMES ARE NOT SEAT ANSWERS. *** While closing #463's stages I reported research at 9/9; it was 8/9. The `codex` entry on that stage is a **`[HELD AWAITING SEAT:` MARKER** -- a record that the seat is OUTSTANDING -- and I counted it because I counted seat NAMES. `check_stage_panels.py` excludes marker entries deliberately, and its own comment says exactly why: *'otherwise marking a gap would close it.'* **Writing down that a seat is missing would, under a name-count, make the stage look complete** -- the seat-failure-as-agreement shape in its purest mechanical form. **THE LEDGER CARRIES 44 SUCH MARKER ENTRIES**, each one a seat that has NOT answered. Any future census of panel coverage that counts names rather than answers over-reports by up to that much. Three marker tokens exist and all three must be excluded: `[HELD AWAITING SEAT:`, `[NOT A PANEL STAGE: SINGLE-SEAT RE-READ]`, and `[RUN UNDER THE PRE-2026-08-16 POLICY]`. *This belongs with the schema-semantics finding rather than beside it: `entries` is not a list of answers, it is a list of EVENTS, and some events record an absence. That is the same present-tense/past-tense confusion that `state` and `closure.note` embody, one level down.* *** A NEW INSTANCE OF THIS ROW'S OWN DEFECT, FOUND 2026-08-25 BY THE ADJUDICATOR TRIPPING OVER IT WHILE ADJUDICATING THIS VERY BLOCK. *** Asked to rule on the queue, the fable5 seat reported that `idesync` "is already closed as document-do-not-fix". The ledger says `state = "in work"` with `commits` EMPTY. Both readings are half right, and the shape is new: *** THE DISPOSITION IS SETTLED BUT THE DOCUMENT HAS NOT SHIPPED. *** The row carries an opus5 REVIEW verdict (2026-08-20) of DOCUMENT-DO-NOT-FIX on a deciding fact nobody else raised -- the drive never advertises FLUSH CACHE, so the highest IDENTIFY word written never sets it -- plus a closed assess stage (`closure.by = fable5`, `CLOSE (assess)`). A SUBSTANCE reader therefore sees a finished decision and says "closed"; a STATE reader sees no commits and says "unfinished". Under the semantics now written, `closed` means discharged BY WORK, and a documenting commit IS work that has not happened -- so the state field is RIGHT and the adjudicator was WRONG, while the adjudicator was right about the only thing anyone would act on. *** THE LESSON IS THAT `document-do-not-fix` NEEDS ITS OWN DISCHARGE, AND NOTHING TRACKS IT. *** A row in this state is invisible to both readings: it looks decided to anyone reading the verdict and claimed to anyone reading the state, so nobody ships the document. That is an UNDISCHARGED OBLIGATION with no carrier -- the class section I of precommit exists for, one field over. Candidate fix, NOT applied pending ratification: `closed` requires either a commit or an explicit `documented-only` closure badge, so an assessed-not-changed record cannot close without the record existing. The project's ethos already demands honest 'assessed, not changed' records; what is missing is anything that NOTICES when one was promised and never written.open

asicarraygeomasicarraygeom shrinking a modelled array to [2] scores a CLEAN SWEEP -- no row verifies the struct declaration the whole invariant rests onasicarraygeom shrinking a modelled array to [2] scores a CLEAN SWEEP -- no row verifies the struct declaration the whole invariant rests on — witness: MEASURED, and the closing row is already BUILT -- _scratchpad/kill463_opus/probe_Mshrink.raw (12/12 escape) and closing_20260825_0334/ (the row that kills it) — note: FOUND BY THE OPUS 5 SEAT on `#463`'s single capped ask-again, alongside the `+1` translation escape. `uint32_t mask_13[3];` -> `mask_13[2];` -- **one character** -- and the 12-row detector scored a CLEAN 12/12. Measured, not reasoned; base and an `& 7` control were run in the same table and the control reproduced `#463`'s own row for row. *** IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED, AND THE REASONING IS THE POINT, because its closing row was ALREADY BUILT AND MEASURED -- which is exactly what made filing it require discipline. *** It fails the de-escalation clause's membership test: apply the shrink to the PRE-FIX code and r = 2 passes the old `if (r == 3)` guard, so the out-of-bounds access was silent under the original code too -- `#463`'s deletion de-announced NOTHING about array geometry, so no accept obligation attaches. It is also outside the depends-on enumeration (it edits a DEFINITION -- the array bound -- and definitions are never inside), and outside even the corrected contract, which claims the bound on `r`, not the bound on the arrays. With the detector shipped, L1 is unavailable. **"Built and works" was never a license**, and every shipped row enlarges the re-measure surface of every future kill table -- measured repeatedly in this project. THE CLOSING ROW, ready to lift: `m13w2x11w0` writes +0x18 and +0x20 and reads back +0x18, wanting 0xc3; under the shrink it reads 0xd4. It would additionally pin `case 0x20:`, one of the five labels the probe header lists as pinned by nothing. THE GENERAL GAP, which is larger than this mutant: **the detector verifies the INDEX and never the ARRAY it indexes into.** The whole invariant is 'r indexes uint32_t[3]', and the [3] half is asserted by the struct declaration alone, which no row reads. Disclosed as out-of-contract in the probe docstring (honesty clause iii). Related: `asicarray4` proposes padding the arrays to [4], which would change what this mutant even means.open

ledgerclosurebyledgerclosureby closure.by holds the WRONG KIND of value on two rows, and a role distinction the roster does not model on ten moreledgerclosureby closure.by holds the WRONG KIND of value on two rows, and a role distinction the roster does not model on ten more — witness: none needed -- the ledger is the artifact; every value is quoted below — note: *** THIS ROW CARRIES OWNER-RATIFIED AMENDMENT 2 OF 2026-08-25 (model the main-loop hat on `closure.by`, plus roster validation), AND DID NOT SAY SO UNTIL 2026-08-29. *** `state_semantics._AMENDMENT_2` recorded that amendment as "tracked as `closurebyroster`" -- **a row id that has never existed in this ledger.** The substance was always here; only the pointer was wrong, so the ratification was invisible from the row that owes it. A row that does not know it is discharging an owner decision gets ranked as a records nit, which is how a ratified obligation goes quiet -- the precise failure the amendment's own closing sentence warns about. FOUND 2026-08-25 while doing the `ledgerstatelies` substance reads, by a check NO SEAT PROPOSED: comparing every `closure.by` value against the roster the ledger itself declares. **A field filled with the WRONG KIND of thing passes every non-empty check there is**, which is why nothing caught it -- section L, the witness check and the closure.by census all only ask whether the field is populated. Five non-roster values, and they are THREE DIFFERENT THINGS -- the count alone would have been misleading, which is the seventh time this session a raw count needed a validity rule before it meant anything: (1) **NOT DEFECTS -- a real distinction the roster does not model.** `fable5-mainloop` (6 rows) and `opus5-mainloop` (4) record that the adjudication happened in the MAIN LOOP rather than in the seat. The carrier is explicit that these are distinct hats and that adjudication DEGRADES to the main loop when a seat is down -- so the suffix is carrying information the bare roster cannot. **The defect is that the schema does not model the hat, not that these ten rows are wrong.** (2) **A SPELLING VARIANT.** `opus` on `strad`, against a roster containing `opus5`. Normalised in place with its warrant. (3) **WRONG KIND ENTIRELY (2 rows).** `measurement` on `lethalonly` names a METHOD; `gen_dashboard.py` on `witnessinvisible` names a FILE. Neither is a party who could adjudicate, and `witnessinvisible` additionally has NO adjudicating entry to derive a correct value from -- so it cannot be repaired by inference, only by someone deciding. PROPOSED FIX, deliberately not applied: model the hat explicitly -- `closure.by` names a roster seat, plus a sibling flag for main-loop-vs-seat -- and have the checker validate closure.by against the roster. That is a schema change and belongs with the `state_semantics` ratification, not ahead of it. *** THE SWEEP WAS WIDENED TO EVERY FIELD, AND THE GOOD NEWS IS THE BOUND: THE PROBLEM IS CONFINED TO `closure.by`. *** Having found one field holding the wrong KIND of value, the obvious question is whether others do. Checked mechanically against what each field is supposed to hold: **`state` 0 outside its vocabulary, `witness` 0 without a ladder prefix, `badge` 0 outside {A, s}.** `commits` flagged TWO rows holding a non-hex token -- `deadman` ('outside the repo (ops)') and `pkbrief` ('ops (panel.sh, outside the repo)') -- and **both are legitimate and are better than a hash would be**: their work predates the harness moving into git on 2026-08-17, so no commit exists, and the field SAYS SO in words. An empty field would be ambiguous between 'no commits' and 'not recorded'; a fake hash would be worse still. Not defects. *That makes it the EIGHTH time in one session that a raw count needed a validity rule before it meant anything -- '2 non-hex commits' is 0 defects -- and the first time the rule was applied BEFORE the number was reported anywhere.*open

A citation is consumed only by a READER, and a reader using one opens the file, so a drifted number SELF-REFUTES AT THE POINT OF USE. A carried count does not. That is why all eight were caught by a seat or a re-read. *** THE REMEDY HAS BEEN ADOPTED FOUR SEPARATE TIMES, EACH ROUND-LOCAL, NEVER CARRIED -- the `countderiver` 'already shipping, uncodified' shape exactly. *** The #340-era round (*'replaced by symbol-anchored citations instead of a third set of numbers'*), #408 (*'every citation now names the construct'*), the fourth-instance note (*'the arms are named by what they ARE'*), and my own grep-anchor conversion today. **Section D1's own header already says 'prefer naming the CONSTRUCT over the line'.** The class keeps re-biting because each adoption stayed inside one round's records. **THE RULE, NOW STANDING RATHER THAN ROUND-LOCAL:** line numbers only ACROSS files, with the qualifier ON the citation; SAME-FILE references positional or by CONSTRUCT NAME; durable cross-file references as VERIFIED-UNIQUE grep anchors. **It removes the measured population -- 7 of 8 instances were same-file or bare forms the rule eliminates outright** -- and it is structure in the sense that matters: it lives where citations are WRITTEN and fails at the point of USE, because an anchor that matches nothing is loud. **PRE-SPECIFIED ESCALATION, so nobody re-argues it: the first MEASURED decision consumed by a stale line citation -- a fix mis-aimed by one, a gate passing falsely, a seat verifying green against wrong content -- converts the form rule into an anchor-verification check bounded to ADDED citations, forward-only from a cutoff. It audits nothing retroactively and builds nothing until that trigger fires.** *** TWO MORE INSTANCES 2026-08-26, BRINGING THE RECORDED COUNT TO EIGHT -- AND THE SECOND IS THE WORST SHAPE THIS CLASS HAS PRODUCED. *** **(7) A CORRECTION NOTE WENT STALE INSIDE THE COMMIT THAT WROTE IT.** #465's probe gained a note reading *":720 is :733, :475-480 is :486-494"*. Re-derived: `d->cond = idata;` is at **:736** -- :733 was true at `4d05cf0` and was invalidated by `5b5089d`, **the very commit carrying the note** -- and the tail is :491-496, which was NEVER right, since even at `4d05cf0` it began at :488. Fourth generation of drift on one file: pre-fix numbers, invalidated; a note written against the previous commit, invalidated again. **(8) AND THE FIX FOR (7) WAS DEFEATED BY ITS OWN EXPLANATION.** The repair stripped the `panel_` prefix from a backlog list so the names could not false-cite -- then wrote the full name in the sentence EXPLAINING the circularity, so it false-cited anyway. Caught by the count moving 78 -> 77 only after a second pass. *** THE REMEDY IS NOW MEASURED, NOT PROPOSED: RE-KEY TO GREP ANCHORS. *** Six drifted carrier citations were converted to greppable tokens earlier the same day (`grep -n 'LOGDIR/mutation'`, `'rm -rf "$dir"'`, the "honour $LOGDIR" comment, gate_hygiene's own "READS THE RAW PTY LOGS ON PURPOSE" header) and **each was verified to resolve UNIQUELY** -- because a key that matches nothing is worse than the stale number it replaced, which I then proved by shipping an anchor that matched ZERO and having to fix it. *** AND THE DIAGNOSIS THE ROW WAS MISSING: THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS AND IS BLIND BY CONSTRUCTION. *** `precommit_check.sh` section D extracts every added `file.c:NNN` and checks the file has at least that many lines. **Its own success message says so: "cited $c exists (READ THE LINE -- existence is not correctness)".** So `:733` passed GREEN today -- the file has more than 733 lines -- while the content had moved to `:736`. That is the third check-that-cannot-fail-for-its-class found in one day. **A BOUNDED STRENGTHENING IS AVAILABLE, and it is verified against the real instance:** for each added `file.ext:NNN`, if THAT FILE IS ALSO MODIFIED BY THE SAME DIFF, warn -- the commit's own hunks move the lines, so the citation is at risk BY CONSTRUCTION. **MEASURED: `git show --name-only 5b5089d` lists `src/devices/dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c`, so the rule fires on today's case.** It must be a WARN and not a FAIL: correctness is undecidable, and a self-citation into an edited file is sometimes right. Cost is a few lines beside the existing D loop. NOT BUILT -- put to the adjudicator, because it changes a checker every commit runs and owes negative controls in both directions (a same-file citation into an edited file must WARN; one into an untouched file must stay silent). The carrier already states the rule (*'a line number in a comment is invalidated by your own edits to that file; re-grep every same-file citation AFTER the last edit'*). **#463 broke it SIX TIMES while knowing it**, which is the argument for mechanising rather than restating: (1) `:200,:203` for the debug() calls, stale when the #463 comment was first inserted; (2) the SAME cite stale AGAIN after the comment was trimmed three lines shorter -- **a correction that went stale a second time**; (3) `:230` for `default:` in the round block, found by a records-audit seat; (4) `:144-152` for the mask_13 handler in the probe docstring; (5) four BARE artifact names with seven candidates each -- citation decay by NAMESPACE rather than by movement, caught by section X; (6) `:227` for `default:` going stale inside the very edit that corrected a different overstatement. *** THE SHAPE IS ALWAYS THE SAME AND ALWAYS INVISIBLE: the text does not change and stops being true. *** Section D checks that ADDED citations EXIST; it cannot see a citation that still resolves to a line of the wrong content, and existence is not correctness -- its own output says so. PROPOSED CHECK, cheap and mechanical: for each `:NNN` in a source comment, require an adjacent ANCHOR TOKEN (a short quoted fragment of the cited line) and verify the token is actually ON line NNN. That converts every citation into a self-verifying pair and catches movement, trimming and namespace decay alike. Cost: one token per citation, and the round that wrote six stale ones would have caught all six at commit time. *** A SEVENTH INSTANCE, AND IT PRODUCED A BETTER FIX THAN THE CHECKER THIS ROW PROPOSED. *** Adding seven lines about transaction closure moved `default:` again, and `:229` came to point at `d->mask_9[r] = idata;`. Caught only because the citation was re-derived immediately after the edit -- the manual discipline works exactly as long as someone remembers it, which is the definition of a check that eventually does not happen. **THE REAL FIX IS CHEAPER THAN AN ANCHOR-TOKEN CHECKER: a SAME-FILE citation does not need a line number.** `default:` is in the same function, below the comment; `the default: arm below` and `the struct above` are unambiguous, need no maintenance, and CANNOT DECAY -- there is nothing there to go stale. Applied: all same-file `:NNN` citations in this comment are now positional, and the only numbers left are CROSS-FILE -- and the ENUMERATION here named four when there are SIX (`core/debugmsg.c:375`, `core/debugmsg.c:384-390`, `cpu_sh_instr.c:790-798`, `dreamcast_sysasicvar.h:72`, `dreamcast_sysasicvar.h:74`, `configure:312-314`); the CLAIM that all remaining are cross-file is true and zero bare `:NNN` remain, but the list was not exhaustive -- which edits to THIS file cannot move. **THE RULE THAT FALLS OUT: cite a line number only ACROSS files; within a file, cite by POSITION or by the name of the thing.** That removes the entire class from same-file comments at zero cost, and leaves the checker worth building for the cross-file remainder, which is a much smaller surface -- seven instances this round were ALL same-file. *** AN EIGHTH INSTANCE, AND THIS ONE REFUTES A JUDGEMENT RATHER THAN AN EDIT. *** After converting every same-file citation to a positional reference, two bare cross-file numbers remained, each following a QUALIFIED cite to the same file. I inspected them and judged the idiom clear enough -- `core/debugmsg.c:384-390, against debug()'s at :375`. **A pass-2 seat then read `:375` as a SAME-FILE citation and reported claim 3 as failing**, with a second seat independently flagging one `:NNN` it 'cannot prove cross-file'. **The judgement was refuted by demonstration, which is stronger than any argument I had for it**: the question was never whether the idiom CAN be read correctly but whether it IS, and two of six readers did not. Fixed by repeating the filename rather than relying on proximity. THE RULE SHARPENS: **a citation's qualifier must be ON the citation, not merely NEAR it.** Proximity is not qualification -- it depends on the reader carrying context across a line break, which is exactly what a reader skimming a 60-line comment does not do.open
