See the correction below. — note: *** FOUND 2026-08-25 WHILE VERIFYING A PREMISE IN THE `gdrompionull` PASS-1 BRIEF, NOT WHILE LOOKING FOR IT. *** The brief's Q4 asked, almost as an afterthought, whether `d->cur_data_offset` is reset anywhere -- because the round had reasoned about `data_len` throughout and barely looked at the guard's OTHER operand. It is reset (`:327`, beside the NULL). But reading the guard to check that showed something else. *** THE GUARD CHECKS ONE BYTE AND THE BODY READS TWO. *** Verified by reading, three lines: (1) `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:611` -- `if (d->cur_data_offset < d->data_len) {` (2) `:612-613` -- `odata = d->data[d->cur_data_offset ++];` then `odata |= (d->data[d->cur_data_offset ++] << 8);` -- **two increments, one bounds test** (3) `alloc_data` `:309` -- `malloc(d->data_len)`, **exactly `data_len` bytes, no padding, no rounding**. So at `cur_data_offset == data_len - 1` the guard PASSES, the first read is the last valid byte, and **the second read is `d->data[data_len]` -- one byte past the allocation**. *** REACHABILITY, STATED AS WHAT IS READ AND WHAT IS OWED. *** READ: `data_len = d->cnt` (`:307`), and `d->cnt` is GUEST-WRITABLE A BYTE AT A TIME -- `:704` sets the low byte from a CNTLO store and `:712` the high byte from CNTHI, so an ODD count is expressible. The two subsequent adjustments do not remove oddness: `:409-410` only replaces `cnt` when it is ZERO, and `:486-487` only rewrites the single value 65536. **OWED: a measurement that an odd `cnt` actually survives to `alloc_data` on a path a guest can drive.** The existing `gdrom_pio_null_probe.py` already stages commands through these registers and could answer it with two extra stores; I have NOT run it, and this row does not claim the defect is reachable until that runs. *** WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT FROM `gdrompionull` AND MUST NOT BE FOLDED INTO IT. *** That row is `data` NULL while `data_len` lies -- a state-invariant violation whose fix is one assignment in the tail. This is an OFF-BY-ONE in a bounds test, on a path where `data` is a perfectly valid pointer and `data_len` is honest. Different fix design (`< data_len` becomes `+ 1 < data_len`, or the read becomes width-aware), different oracle (a heap over-read, not a SIGSEGV), so under the reopening rule they are separate rounds. **Note the two interact in the safe direction: `gdrompionull`'s fix sets `data_len = 0`, under which this guard is false and the over-read cannot occur on THAT path.** It does nothing for the odd-count path. *** AND UNLIKE THIS DEVICE'S OTHER OUT-OF-BOUNDS ISSUES, ASan SHOULD SEE THIS ONE. *** The file's own comment at `:272` records that ASan cannot detect its member-to-member overrun because that is intra-object inside one malloc. **This is a read PAST a malloc'd buffer's end**, which is the case ASan is built for -- so `build-asan/` is a real second oracle here, where for the aliasing family it was not. That is worth testing early because it is cheap and because a positive ASan result would settle reachability and severity in one run. SEVERITY, stated honestly and NOT inflated: a ONE-BYTE heap over-READ. It does not write, and the byte it returns goes to the guest as the high half of a 16-bit read. That is an information leak of one adjacent heap byte per odd-length transfer and a potential crash only if the allocation ends exactly on a page boundary. It is materially less severe than the SIGSEGV in `gdrompionull` and should rank below it. *** REACHABILITY SETTLED 2026-08-25, THE SAME DAY THIS ROW WAS FILED, AND IT SETTLED AGAINST THE ROW. *** The filing said the odd-count route was OWED and explicitly did NOT claim the defect was reachable. That was the right caution, and the answer is NO. *** `data_len` HAS EXACTLY ONE WRITER, AND BOTH ROUTES TO IT FORCE AN EVEN VALUE. *** Verified by grepping every assignment: `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:307` in `alloc_data` (`d->data_len = d->cnt;`) is the only one -- the apparent second hit at `:413` is a printf FORMAT STRING, not an assignment, which is the kind of match that would have made this look open if counted rather than read. `alloc_data` has exactly two call sites and each is guarded: * `:342`, the Read-TOC path, is preceded by `:338-341` -- `if (d->cnt != 408) { fatal(...); exit(1); }`. **408 is even**, and nothing else reaches this call. * `:418`, the read-sectors path, is preceded by `:412-415` -- `if (sector_count * 2048 != d->cnt) { fatal(...); break; }`. **Any multiple of 2048 is even.** Note `:409-410` only substitutes a count when `cnt == 0`, so a guest-set odd count survives THAT line -- and is then rejected by the equality check two lines later. **So the guest CAN express an odd `cnt` at the CNTLO/CNTHI registers (:704, :712), and that half of the filing was right; what it cannot do is get that value past either guard into `alloc_data`.** *** DISPOSITION: LATENT, NOT LIVE. SEVERITY DROPS FROM A ONE-BYTE HEAP OVER-READ TO A STRUCTURAL HAZARD WITH NO ROUTE. *** The asymmetry itself is untouched and still worth recording: `:611` guards `cur_data_offset < data_len` and `:612-613` reads TWO bytes, while `alloc_data` mallocs exactly `data_len` with no padding. **Any future edit that admits an odd length -- a new command arm, a relaxed guard, a different transfer size -- makes this live immediately, and the code carries nothing that would stop it.** That is a real thing to know and a cheap thing to fix (`+ 1 < data_len`, or make the read width-aware), but it is NOT a defect a guest can reach today and this row may not be ranked as one. *** AND THE ASan NOTE IN THE FILING IS NOW MOOT AND IS WITHDRAWN. *** It said `build-asan/` would be a real second oracle here, unlike the intra-object aliasing family. True in principle and irrelevant in fact: ASan cannot observe an access no execution reaches. *Process note worth keeping: this row was filed with reachability marked OWED rather than asserted, and the owed check refuted it within the hour -- at the cost of two greps. Had it been filed as a live heap over-read it would have been a WRONG RECORD ranked above real work, and the correction would have arrived later and cost more.*open

The shipped behaviour is deliberate and is pinned by the `unimpl 2op` row, which fires TWO different opcodes and demands ONE line. — note: *** FILED 2026-08-26 BECAUSE THE SHIPPED DETECTOR'S CONTRACT CLAIMED A FILING THAT DID NOT EXIST. *** `wdc_flood_probe.py`'s header says *"deepseek argued for a per-opcode set; FILED, not shipped"* -- and no row carried it; the only trace was prose inside `wdcflood`'s state_note, which is not something a reader can find. **A contract line asserting a disposition is a WRONG RECORD until the disposition exists as a row.** Caught by the readiness adjudication before the round shipped. THE PROPOSAL, from the deepseek seat on the `wdcflood` pass-1 panel: `:583`'s diagnostic VALUE is the opcode, so a single per-device flag suppresses every later unimplemented command and hides distinct guest actions. A 256-bit set (`uint32_t warned_unimpl_cmd[8]`) is cheap and preserves them. WHY IT WAS NOT SHIPPED, and the reason is not that it is wrong: the scalar is exactly what stops a guest cycling 0x00..0xff for 256 lines, which is the flood the round exists to bound. Per-opcode-versus-per-device is a SPEC choice between two acceptable behaviours, and the adjudication ruled that clause (d) tests the CHOSEN spec's repair rather than adjudicating between specs -- deepseek's framing ("the scalar IS the (d) mutant") is circular, since it assumes per-opcode is the baseline and then calls the alternative a weakening. *** THE SHIPPED SPEC IS PINNED, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS SAFE TO DEFER: *** the `unimpl 2op` row fires TWO DIFFERENT opcodes and demands ONE line, so a later change to per-opcode is a VISIBLE spec change that reddens a row, not a silent drift. The same row kills a "last-warned-opcode" latch (measured: `M3`, 21/22, that row alone), under which an alternating guest floods forever. IF IT IS EVER WORKED, the option set is THREE-membered and the third member is the one the dispute never named: scalar (shipped), per-opcode set (deepseek), and the in-tree COUNT-BOUND idiom (`n_trunc_msgs`, `src/cpus/memory_rw.c:495-523`). Note also that #337's other latched messages at `:816`/`:855` carry NO value payload, so "three latches in this file" is weaker precedent for discarding value-resolution than it looks -- `:583` is the only site whose message names an opcode.open

wdcexpecteddatawdcexpecteddata an EXPECTED DATA write has no quiet pin, so dropping !write_in_progress would warn-and-latch on legal I/O with every detector row greenwdcexpecteddata an EXPECTED DATA write has no quiet pin, so dropping !write_in_progress would warn-and-latch on legal I/O with every detector row green — witness: none -- building it needs a WRITE-command staging sequence `wdc_flood_probe.py` does not have, which is why it is filed rather than fixed. — note: *** RAISED BY THE grok SEAT ON THE `wdcflood` PASS-2 PANEL AND RECORDED NOWHERE UNTIL THE READINESS ADJUDICATION FOUND IT DROPPED. *** The unexpected-DATA-write site is guarded by `!d->write_in_progress && !d->atapi_cmd_in_progress`. **Drop the first conjunct and the site warns-and-latches on a perfectly legal write during an active transfer** -- and every row in the 22-row detector stays GREEN, because none of them stages a WRITE command. *** THIS IS THE ACCEPT-SIDE HOLE THE OTHER THREE QUIET PINS CANNOT COVER. *** `accept ec`, `accept w8` and `accept r8` pin legal COMMAND, legal narrow WRITE and legal narrow READ. None of them puts the device into `write_in_progress`, so the one predicate whose accept side is guest-reachable during real I/O has no pin at all. COST OF CLOSING IT: a WRITE-command staging sequence (set up a 0x30 WRITE, reach DRQ, then store to DATA), which is materially more than the one-or-two-instruction stimuli every other row uses. That is the honest reason it is filed -- not that it does not matter. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY IT REVEALS, which generalises past this row: a latch's accept side is only as good as the STATES the detector can reach, and a detector built from cheap stimuli systematically under-covers predicates that depend on expensive state.open

Its `_probe.py` suffix means classifying it as `tool` trips the checker's MISFILED rule, while classifying it as a detector demands a gate or an exemption it should never have. **It is a file with no honest class.** *** AND I PUT IT THERE. *** It was preserved this morning under the `preserveinstrument` rule -- filed one hour earlier, applied on its first opportunity. **My fix for one row created the conflict that blocks the fix for another**, and neither row could see it: the population is exactly TWO nested probes, the gated detector and the instrument I archived. **SO THE PROJECT'S OWN 'do not alarm on the rest of the class' OBJECTION APPLIES HERE, and the seat said so explicitly** -- the naive fix would force an archival file into a false choice between MISFILED and UNWIRED. **The recommendation is all-or-nothing: land a complete path-aware fix WITH an explicit `research`/`nonshipping` classification, or do not land it. Do not land only re-key + `walk`.** THREE SELF-TEST CONTROLS SPECIFIED, for the file's existing 18-mutant `--selftest` harness: * **NESTED GREEN** -- the unmodified copied tree must show the nested detector as RUN by its gate, not IGNORED or UNWIRED. * **NESTED RED** -- delete its real invocation from the copied gate; require exit 1 naming the FULL RELATIVE PATH as UNWIRED. * **COLLISION** -- add a second classified detector with the SAME BASENAME in a different subdirectory, gate only the original, require the second to remain UNWIRED. **A regression back to basename keying would incorrectly turn BOTH green** -- which is the silent failure the re-key exists to prevent. *Checked: NO same-basename collision exists in `regress/` today, so that hazard is PROSPECTIVE. The existing duplicate-literal guard still works with path keys, provided `exec_sites()` is path-keyed too.* **DISPOSITION: still worth fixing** -- the seat was asked whether it might not be, and answered that `#465`'s escape is direct evidence the blind spot matters even though today's detector is now wired by hand. But it is a LARGER change than the row implied, and shipping half of it is worse than shipping none. *** THIS IS THE STRUCTURAL LANDING SPOT FOR #465's HEADLINE LESSON, AND THE ROUND MISSED IT. *** #465 found that its detector was wired into NO GATE, recorded 'a detector no gate runs is not a detector', and discharged it by a HUMAN GREP. **The mechanical check for exactly that class already exists and was BLIND BY SCOPE** -- `gdrompionull` lived at `regress/artifacts/gdrompionull/`, one level down, where the checker cannot look. **So the round wrote its lesson as prose while the structure that should have carried it sat one directory away, silently not covering the case.** That is the carrier's structure-first rule failing in its own terms, and it is a CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL for a whole subtree -- the class this project named twice today (`panel.sh`'s phantom re-fire, `grok models` as a tier check). **EXPOSURE IS ZERO TODAY, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS FILED AND NOT FIXED IN-ROUND:** 1 of 57 tracked `regress/**.py` sat below top level, and it is now gated by hand. The defect is latent, not live. THE FIX, as the seat scoped it: re-key `MANIFEST`/`EXEMPT` from BASENAME to RELATIVE PATH and replace `os.listdir` with `os.walk`. **It owes negative controls in both directions** -- prove a subdirectory detector with no gate is now RED, and prove a gated one stays GREEN -- and the file already carries an 18-mutant `--selftest` harness to hang them on. A basename->path re-key can silently collide (two files with the same basename in different directories), so that needs its own row. *A checker whose docstring overclaims its scope is worse than one that admits a limit: the docstring is what a future round reads when deciding whether the class is already covered.*in work

Correct, suffix-aware: **174 dirs / 78 cited / 96 uncited.** My first attempt used a loose `panel_*` glob that matched `.out` FILES (229/157); my 'correction' then required `panel_<8>_<6>` EXACTLY, which silently dropped **eight real dirs carrying suffixes** (`..._024101_audit`, `..._044509_ledger11`, `..._110328_0798b90_pass2` and five more). I wrote a filter instead of reading the one that works. **(2) THE ACTIONABLE SET IS EIGHT, NOT FOUR.** Four on 08-24, and FOUR MORE ON 08-25 that my exact-match filter could not see: `diffrec`, `ledger11`, `tailfacts`, and `0798b90_pass2`. **Two are heavyweight** (ledger11 carries a 1.29 MB codex answer; diffrec 1.07 MB) and **one is a PASS 2 ON A SHIPPED SOURCE-TOUCHING COMMIT** -- precisely the late-dissent shape where an unharvested answer reads as false unanimity. **(3) THE OVERSTATEMENT WAS ~12x, NOT ~4x.** 96 uncited against 8 actionable. *** (4) MY OWN NOTE MADE AN UNCITED DIR LOOK CITED, WHICH IS A DEFECT SHAPE I HAVE NOT SEEN BEFORE. *** The first draft listed that dir's name in full (prefix included), so a suffix-aware grep found it in the ledger and scored it CITED -- **on the strength of the sentence saying it was uncited.** A record ABOUT an unread review made the review look read. The adjudicator hit this too: its own first census scored that dir cited for the same reason. **RESOLVED BY STRIPPING THE `panel_` PREFIX in the backlog list below**, so the names stay human-readable and greppable-by-timestamp while NOT matching the citation pattern. *The adjudicator asked for the names in full; written in full they re-create the circularity, so this takes the instruction's intent -- make them findable -- by a form that cannot false-cite.* THE BACKLOG (prefix stripped deliberately; prepend `panel_` to open them): 20260824_030624 5 substantial answers 20260824_034510 5 20260824_041606 7 20260824_124655 6 20260825_032831_diffrec codex 1.07 MB, minimax 61 KB 20260825_044509_ledger11 codex 1.29 MB, deepseek 281 KB, seven seats 20260825_100232_tailfacts MARGINAL -- two sub-2 KB answers; may close by annotation 20260825_110328_0798b90_pass2 *** pass 2 on a SHIPPED commit *** **THE CUTOFF IS RE-WARRANTED, because the reason I filed was an unchecked absence claim** -- the class this project mandates checking rather than asserting. I wrote 'older dirs belong to closed rounds whose findings WERE acted on' and checked none of them. The adjudicator checked THREE across two eras and found every finding ABSORBED: `20260822_184955`'s headline mutant is the shipped accept-row kill with its delivery rows in the gate; `20260823_140419`'s '(once per offset)' edit is in `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` verbatim at four sites; `20260813_183758`'s open question lives as the held `dfreq` row. **n=3, zero live misses** -- which supports refusing the 96-sweep on evidence instead of on convenience. So the cutoff is not 'three days'. It is **2026-08-24, the citation rule's own adoption date, forward-only** -- the same dated-cutoff idiom as `HOLDQ_CUTOFF` and `check_bugfile_sync`'s `CUTOFF`. Older dirs stay under the read-side rule: re-derive before leaning, file anything found decayed. **Note the uncited population is NOT confined to the pre-ledger age** (08-22 has 12 of 17 uncited, 08-23 six of 12), so the cutoff is a policy line, not a natural one. **PRE-SPECIFIED, so the sample size is honest: a sample of three is not a proof. If the eight-dir harvest finds even ONE live unacted finding, sample the 08-22/23 band (18 dirs) before closing this row. If zero, close it and record the sample.** *** (5) AND THE ROW'S OWN FRAMING WAS OVERSTATED, REFUTED BY MY OWN COMMIT BODY. *** It said every unread-review instance that day was 'a finding sitting in a seat answer nobody had opened'. Commit `087a786` says of the largest instance, verbatim: *'not a review nobody read, but a review I read thoroughly and left unrecorded'*. **Today's instances are predominantly RECORDING gaps, not unopened findings.** The 'twice cost a full round to rediscover' clause is true of the HISTORICAL instances -- the kimi member-2 answer, `m8invpred` -- not of today's. That is the dropped-qualifier class: evidence for one case restated as a property of the day. *** AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS VERY FIX WAS DEFEATED BY ITS OWN EXPLANATION. *** I stripped the `panel_` prefix from the backlog list, then wrote the full name in the sentence EXPLAINING the circularity -- so the dir was still scored cited. That is the correction-quotes-what-it-refutes hazard, documented in the carrier this same morning as the reason a naive stale-text grep *gets steadily more wrong as the file gets more honest*. **Here it defeated a fix inside the paragraph describing the fix.** The rule that follows is narrow and mechanical: **when a record must NAME an artifact it is asserting is UNRECORDED, the name must not be written in the form the checker matches -- anywhere in the record, including the prose about it.**open

loadfragileloadfragile every pty probe waited on an ABSOLUTE deadline, so a merely SLOW run failed identically to a STUCK one -- the battery could only be trusted on an idle machineloadfragile every pty probe waited on an ABSOLUTE deadline, so a merely SLOW run failed identically to a STUCK one -- the battery could only be trusted on an idle machine — witness: harness:selftest_inactivity.py -- proves the property behaviourally against a stub, no rig and no build. Negative-controlled both directions: removing the reset from one probe turns it RED and names the file; restoring goes GREEN. — note: *** PASS 2 ON 29b450c REFUTED THIS ROUND'S SAFETY LEMMA, TWO SEATS INDEPENDENTLY. *** I wrote that the inactivity deadline *'cannot turn a passing run into a failing one'* and presented it as the whole safety argument. **It is correct and INCOMPLETE, which is worse than wrong because it reads as a proof.** codex: *'monotonic for successful runs, but not failure-safe; noisy failure defeats the bound.'* kimi, independently: *'both failure directions exist.'* **THE HONEST PROPERTY: monotonic for SUCCESSFUL runs, UNBOUNDED for NOISY FAILURES.** A run that fails while still producing output never trips the deadline at all. A run that hangs SILENTLY is still caught -- which is the case the deadline was written for, so the change is still right; the CLAIM was over-general. **TWO MORE OVERCLAIMS -- AND CHECKING THEM CORRECTED MY OWN CORRECTION.** An earlier draft of this note said both were *'corrected in the round block'*. **Neither was IN the round block.** Verified: the CHANGELOG already says *'Scope is two probes ... the remaining ~245 sites are FILED as `loadfragile`'*, and it never claims `free_run` is the ONLY absolute window -- it only explains why that one is not converted. * *'changes every pty probe deadline'* -- **that was in MY BRIEF, not the record.** It changes TWO. codex caught it as a contradiction between my prose and my own CHANGELOG, which means the CHANGELOG was the half that was right. * *'`free_run` is the only intentional absolute window'* -- **also the brief.** There is another: `max_drain_s` in `run_arm`, which bounds and measures the whole drain phase. I claimed completeness on an enumeration I had not finished. *So the shipped RECORD was accurate on scope and my BRIEF was not -- which is the opposite of what I first wrote here. A correction block earns the same scrutiny as the thing it corrects; this one did not get it until the anchor failed and forced a check.* *** AND A BRIEF DEFECT THAT IS WORSE THAN ANY OF THEM, because it degrades the panel itself: MY BRIEF LABELLED A TRUNCATED EXTRACT 'THE PRODUCT DIFF, verbatim'. *** It carried 78 lines -- the header hunks only -- of a **12-file, 427-insertion** commit, and `#467`'s probe change was ABSENT ENTIRELY while two of my five questions asked about it. **The Ollama seats CANNOT READ FILES. They see only what is inlined.** So calling a truncated extract 'verbatim' does not merely omit -- it tells a packet-fed seat that the omission is the whole thing. kimi caught it by checking the hunk-header arithmetic against what followed, and said so in its verdict line. *Both dissents were worth more than a ratification: they found the guard's negative-domain hole, the incomplete lemma, and three wrong records -- while confirming the code itself is sound.* *** RAISED BY THE OWNER ASKING WHETHER WINDOWS COULD EVER BE IDLE ENOUGH. The honest answer was no -- and that reframes the problem: do not chase idleness, remove the load-sensitivity. *** **MY FIRST FRAMING WAS WRONG AND I CORRECTED IT BEFORE ACTING.** I proposed converting the worst offenders to WORK-ACCOUNTING, on `#419`'s precedent (`LUNA_BUDGET` counts guest instructions, so a loaded host executes the same work and the oracle holds). Classifying the 249 wall-clock references showed that is not the defect: guest-side budgets, already work-accounted 3 pty TRANSPORT timeouts 245 true measurement oracles (the #419 case) 1 **Work-accounting cannot fix a transport timeout**: while you wait for bytes there are no guest instructions to count -- the whole point is you do not know whether the guest is running. Converting literally as proposed would have changed ONE thing. **THE REAL DEFECT, and it is bigger: ZERO files used an inactivity deadline.** Every one read `t = time.time()` once and looped `while time.time() - t < timeout` -- a TOTAL-TIME budget spent by the clock rather than by the guest. A boot that normally takes 40 s and takes 90 s under load FAILS while bytes arrive steadily throughout. **THE FIX: reset the clock when the buffer grows**, so `timeout` means SILENCE. `rd()` cannot report progress -- it returns True both on data and on a quiet select() tick -- so progress is `len(self.buf)` changing. **SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: strictly more permissive for a run that produces output, identical for one that does not. It cannot turn a passing run into a failing one.** *** `free_run(seconds)` IS DELIBERATELY NOT CONVERTED. *** It is not a timeout at all -- it is an EXPOSURE WINDOW that runs the guest for a set period and then SIGINTs. Converting it would change the experiment rather than protect it, **and a naive sweep over `time.time()` sites would have eaten it.** That is why this converts one NAMED method rather than a pattern. DETECTOR SHIPPED WITH THE FIX: `selftest_inactivity.py`, two legs OPPOSITE IN SIGN -- slow-but-progressing (old shape FAILS, new PASSES) and genuinely-stuck (BOTH must still FAIL). **The second leg is the one that matters: a conversion that made the timeout unreachable would sail through the first and defend nothing.** Plus a source leg catching a silent revert. SCOPE: two probes converted -- the measured worst offenders, 7 tight budgets each. The remaining ~245 sites are the same class and are FILED here rather than swept, because each needs the `free_run` distinction checked by hand. *One conversion needed care: `fbpending_drain_probe.py` is one of only two CRLF files in the tree. It was converted PRESERVING its line endings (+16/-0), because normalising would have produced the ~500-line churn diff this session already had to justify once.*in work

The class is NOT 'rows nobody looked at'. It is rows that WERE reviewed, often by a full nine-seat panel, whose conclusion was never written into the row. *** **The numbers, derived from the ledger and re-derivable at any commit** (rule: a count names its deriver). Open rows = state not in {closed, dropped}; *no disposition* = `state_note` under 120 chars AND `closure.note` under 40: ``` open rows 162 by state: held 87 | open 56 | in work 19 open rows with NO disposition in EITHER field 85 of those: held 58 | open 18 | in work 9 ...that nonetheless received seat entries 85 (ALL of them) total seat entries sitting on them 472 ``` **472 seat answers, from all nine seats, on rows whose conclusion is recorded nowhere in the row.** The heaviest are `pitlatch` (30 entries), `pitclobber` (24), `sh4tlbda2` (20), and `arcbiosubsan` / `sh4chcr` / `sh4rtcsr` (18 each). *** TWO MEASURED CONSEQUENCES, BOTH FOUND TODAY, AND THEY ARE THE REASON THIS IS NOT BOOKKEEPING. *** * [[smnotland]] -- assessed REAL by `fable5` on 2026-08-19, and **fixed by `1a85e27` the SAME DAY**. Still open. * [[pitclobber]] -- **fixed by `#439` (`020a672`)**, which also shipped a 308-line detector. Still open. > **An open row describing a fixed defect is worse than an untidy queue: a seat fired on it reviews something that no longer exists, and will either waste the firing or construct an argument for a defect it cannot find.** This is the `sgiarcbiosoob` precedent -- a hold text outliving its own oracle -- now with two more instances in one day. *** METHOD CORRECTIONS, recorded because each one changed the answer and a future sweep will hit them again: *** 1. **`state_note` is the wrong field for HELD rows.** They carry their disposition in `closure.note`. A sweep reading only `state_note` reports `armbdt` and `b120r` as undispositioned when both hold real `fable5` closure notes. The count above reads BOTH. 2. **'Does a commit mention the row id?' looked inert and is not.** It returned 0 of 102, which I first dismissed as zero-recall -- then the negative control showed `smnotland` DOES appear in two commit messages. **The control was what made the zero meaningful**; without it the result would have been discarded, and with it the zero says those rows genuinely have not been worked. **DISPOSITION: work the class by DISPOSITIONING, not by re-reviewing.** The reviews already exist. The cheap, high-yield move on each row is to read its own `entries`, write the conclusion into the row, and close what is already fixed -- and only then decide whether it still needs a round. *** THIS CLASS EXPLAINS TWO OF TODAY'S SURPRISES, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW. *** **A bare title is not nothing** -- it names a defect someone actually saw, and this project's own history says those are real. **But it carries no reachability, no severity and no reproduction**, so a round claiming one must re-derive everything before it can begin. **THE MEASURED COST, both today:** * `verdictprose` was triaged as UNWORKABLE in the morning *because* its note was empty -- I recorded that its evidence 'would need re-deriving from scratch' and moved on. the measurement shows both halves are load-bearing and **neither subsumes the other** -- sharper than the filing knew. **WHERE IT GOES:** `regress/diff_m8invread.c` (778 lines today), which already has the two-cpu / two-CMMU fixture. **~20 lines.** *The entry says a prototype was committed to the artifact dir; Unmodified `evbmips -e malta`, wdc via the committed bus_pci/piix4_ide path, free-running, 1.52 s, 20 of 20 predictions across both legs. Sentinel ADDTOINBUF_RUNG3_DONE. Controls: RAM liveness; a DEVICE SIGNATURE (two reads of one address giving push order, which a cell cannot); encodings 46/46 words AND mnemonics against the emulator's own disassembler; disk content at known offsets. On the committed build the guest is handed ITS OWN INJECTED BYTES back as disk data. — note: *** RIDER FROM THE FABLE SEAT 2026-08-27: THE WRITE-ARM BOUND COVERS MORE THAN DATA CORRUPTION. *** The CDB dispatch keys on ring OCCUPANCY `== 12` while the write arm is unguarded during DATAIN. So a mid-DATAIN write sequence can drive occupancy to exactly 12 and trigger a **SPURIOUS COMMAND DISPATCH, which frees and replaces `atapi_st`** -- while a transfer is live and holding pointers into it. *That is a lifetime hazard, not a data hazard, and it raises this row above 'the guest corrupts its own transfer'. Filed from READING; not measured.* *** FILED BY `#473`, AND ITS RATIONALE WAS CORRECTED THE SAME DAY BY TWO SEATS. *** `#473` bounded the two DATAIN arms. It did NOT bound the primitive: `wdc_addtoinbuf()` has no capacity check and `head == tail` still means BOTH empty and full. **THE FILING SAID "correct and complete for every caller in the tree today". THAT IS IMPRECISE, and both the Fable and grok seats named the same live counter-example independently:** the data-port WRITE arm pushes guest bytes with no phase guard and no capacity check, and its unexpected-write latch is SUPPRESSED precisely because `atapi_cmd_in_progress` is set. Research (fix proposals)·OK2026-08-27 — CONFIRMED — VERDICT: CONFIRMED -- the lost seat's numbers were right, AND THE RE-TAKE FOUND WHAT THE ORIGINAL NEVER RECORDED. The panel's gate is discharged: the warrant no longer rests on an unpreserved artifact. Q1 -- twelve writes to 0x1400002c, six of value 0x08? **YES TO BOTH.** Reproduced on four runs (three pristine boots plus the instrumented build): 12 writes, 0 reads, all len=1, all from pc=0x8c15f6e8 <obio_iomem_write_1+0x8>, all real guest stores (no_exceptions=0). *** Q2 -- THE VALUES, WHICH NO PREVIOUS REPORT CAPTURED, AND ONE OF THEM CARRIES WDCTL_RST. *** 1 0x0c WDCTL_4BIT | WDCTL_RST <-- SRST ASSERTED 2 0x08 WDCTL_4BIT <-- SRST released 3..12 0x02 / 0x08 alternating (IDS / 4BIT, five pairs) histogram: 0x0c x1, 0x08 x6, 0x02 x5 So the FIRST write is a real ATA soft-reset assert/release pair at the head of the channel probe, silently discarded today. Bit names taken from the tree's own src/include/thirdparty/wdcreg.h, not from memory. Confirmed independently ON THE UNMODIFIED BINARY by the tree's committed write-watchpoint (#250): same paddr, 0x0c first, same value set. It saw 9 of 12 because the watchpoint self-suppresses while about_to_enter_single_step is set -- **a lower bound BY CONSTRUCTION**, so it corroborates the VALUES and not the count, and the seat said so rather than reporting 9 as a discrepancy. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX, and it is the question this round has been holding for: mapping the register makes that first write REACH `wdc_new_command_reset()` -- clearing atapi_cmd_in_progress, atapi_phase and write_in_progress, and purging the inbuf ring. On a fresh channel probe those are already zero, so the effect is probably nil HERE; but it is a real state change and the round must say so rather than describe the arm as inert. The 0x08/0x02 writes hit no WDCTL_RST branch. COMMAND_RESET's only two consumers (the cyl_lo/cyl_hi read arms) are both diskimage_is_a_cdrom()-gated and do not fire on this IDE-disk rig. **The fix-side measurement was deliberately NOT taken.** *** Q3 -- THE DISCRIMINATING CONTROL, AND IT DECIDES BETWEEN THE TWO DIAGNOSES: THE COMMAND BLOCK SUCCEEDS. *** 12,718 accesses across all eight registers (2560 DATA reads, 10,033 status polls, 33 sdh writes, 14 commands), and wd0 ATTACHES: 131 cyl / 16 head / 63 sec / 132048 sectors -- a device signature RAM cannot produce. Cross-checked against the pristine build's own -v output, which counts 2560 `wdc: read from DATA`, matching the hook exactly. So the defect is a MISSING OFFSET CASE, not a wrong devinit->addr, and the one-line fix is aimed correctly. Had it come back the other way, the one-liner would have papered over a misplaced device. Q4 -- anything else claiming 0x1400002c? NO, and confirmed on the CONSTRUCTED machine via `device list` rather than by grep alone. And the registered wdc_altstatus at 0x14000206 receives ZERO accesses for the entire boot -- the handler that exists is never reached. *** THE INSTRUMENT TRAP, WHICH IS THE PART THAT OUTLIVES THIS ROW. *** The seat's FIRST census hook reported 12 unmapped writes and ZERO command-block accesses -- clean, confident, and half wrong. The device arm of MEMORY_RW_ONE_PAGE does `paddr -= mem->devices[i].baseaddr` BEFORE calling the handler, so device accesses reach do_return_ok carrying the RELATIVE offset. **A window predicate on `paddr` is therefore blind to exactly the mapped half -- the half that answers Q3.** That is plausibly how the earlier lost report came back with the writes and no control: not a lost log so much as an instrument that could only see one side. It is the phantom-absence class with a subtraction in it, and the fix was an entry-paddr latch plus PROVING THE INSTRUMENT SEES THE POSITIVE CASE BEFORE BELIEVING ITS NEGATIVES. NOT SETTLED, recorded as such: whether delivering the reset changes the boot outcome (fix-side, deliberately untaken); CD-ROM rig behaviour; anything past the installer prompt. All numbers scope to OpenBSD 7.6 RAMDISK #70's probe/attach phase. That bound is deliberate and correct; its own comment says *a gate that hard-fails on a tree someone chose not to build is a gate that gets switched off*. **But a file no round happens to touch is never checked**, so a tree that was already stale when the 2026-08-27 ruling landed stays stale forever. Measured: 111 divergent .c/.h files, of which `diskimage.h` and `makeautodev.sh` broke the build -- neither touched by a recent round. **THE SHAPE, worth stating because it generalises past this tree: an INCREMENTAL sync check cannot detect a stale BASELINE.** The tree passed every commit while compiling nothing. *** THE DECISION: a SOFT-WARNING full `diff -rq` over the .c/.h set, SKIPPED ENTIRELY when the tree is absent. *** Warn, do not hard-fail -- and skip on absence -- so the absence-is-not-a-failure property that keeps this gate switched on is preserved. SCOPE NOTE: `Makefile`s legitimately differ (they carry the ASan COPTIM) and must be excluded; the measured expectation after a correct sync is **14 differing files, all Makefiles, zero others**. `est/` is NOT in scope -- it has a declared divergence allowlist (`tools/est_divergence.txt`); build-asan has none, which is why any .c/.h divergence there is staleness by definition.open

Any path can appear there, `.index` included, because the population comes from git rather than from a find with extension filters. *** SO IF gate_build READ THE FILE VERBATIM, `.index` WOULD ENTER ITS EXPECTED SET, WHERE `list_diffs` CANNOT PRODUCE IT -- AND ITS OWN STALE-ENTRY CHECK WOULD FLAG IT STALE ON EVERY RUN. Permanently red. That is exactly the failure that cost five days and a skipped gate, reintroduced by the repair for it. *** THE ROW'S CORE FINDING SURVIVES AND IS UNCHANGED: gate_build pins its own list, that pinned copy DID go stale, and the staleness cost a red battery plus `gate_mips`. What is refuted is only the proposed remedy and the `.index` evidence for it. TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, neither taken here, both now stated with the constraint they must satisfy: (a) gate_build reads the file but FILTERS to the extensions list_diffs covers, so the expected set and the actual set are drawn from the same population; (b) leave them separate and add a check that gate_build's list is exactly the extension-filtered SUBSET of the file's -- which catches drift without coupling two checks that legitimately differ. *This is the addition licence doing its job before an edit rather than after: the proposed change had no measured delta and no transferred warrant, only 'the two lists disagree, so unify them'. Reading what each list is FOR took minutes and refuted it.* — evidence: direct reading of gate_build.sh's list_diffs() and precommit_check.sh's section A·······

TWO L2 ESCAPES ARE ALREADY MEASURED AGAINST THE ROW SET THE BRIEF PROPOSED. Hand these to the measuring seat as its FIRST assignment, not its ask-again. *** **M1 -- `len != 8 && writeflag == MEM_WRITE`.** Every STORE row stays byte-identically green while ALL SIX READ SITES DIE. Only a TWO-SITES-IN-ONE-SESSION row sees it. PER-SITE LATCHES, with an in-tree warrant rather than a preference.** `dev_wdc.c`'s own comment adjudicates the discriminator: *SIX FLAGS, NOT FOUR* -- sharing is licensed only across sites MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE AT RUNTIME (`#337`'s shared flag spans two arms of one endianness branch). The six sgi_re windows are walked in one session by any driver bringing up the RE, so they are not mutually exclusive. A shared bit reports one window and hides five. **7. THE FIX'S WARRANT IS STRONGER THAN 'UNIMPLEMENTED', BUT NOT AS STRONG AS THIS POINT ORIGINALLY CLAIMED -- CORRECTED IN PLACE 2026-08-30.** It said *'the guard is load-bearing HOST memory safety'*. **MEASURED FALSE by `offsetof`:** the over-run lands INSIDE the same allocation (`re_linear_a[32]` IS `re_linear_b[0]`; `re_linear_b[32]` IS `de_reg[0]`), so it is UB plus SILENT INTRA-STRUCT CROSS-ARRAY CORRUPTION -- not a wild write, not a host crash, and **invisible to plain ASAN**. The phrase survived here after being corrected in `sgilinearoob`, in the very row whose first line tells the implementer to read it before the brief: *corrected in one place, alive in one more*, which is mechanical rule 2's exact scenario. **AND THIS POINT BUNDLED A SECOND, SEPARATELY-UNVERIFIED CLAIM:** the `len == 1` over-read of `data[hwi+1]` is of the CALLER'S buffer, and nobody has established that buffer's size -- so it is not 'host memory safety' either. The honest warrant is **cross-array corruption plus an unverified caller-buffer over-read**, which still settles DECLINE against IMPLEMENT and settles it for reasons that are true. **8. NAME `sgidewidth` IN THE PRETABLE AND ROUND RECORD.** It is a SEVENTH live width kill in the same file, deliberately excluded (different handler, different accept set, readable registers). Eight of nine seats answered; none found anything wrong with the three shipped fixes -- the domain clamp, the catch-up bound, the RTC narrowing and the above-the-early-out placement were each confirmed by every seat that could trace them. b118Lb118L A disk that fails to be added stays on the listb118L A disk that fails to be added stays on the list — HOLD: FILE - no measurable effect until a caller survives — Split from b118. The disk is linked before several failure returns, so a half-built entry can remain. Both callers exit on failure today and a null file pointer is guarded, so a fix has no measurable effect yet. Worth doing when a non-exiting caller appears. — witness: none -- TRUE but NOT OBSERVABLE. Established by reading 2026-08-27: both call sites terminate the process on failure and nothing walks the disk list in between, so no witness at any rung can exist without first adding a caller that survives the error. — note: *** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27, established by READING under the machine embargo -- no build needed, and none would help. *** **THE CLAIM IS TRUE, and the asymmetry is unmistakable rather than arguable.** `diskimage_add()` (`src/disk/diskimage.c:1631-2104`) links the new disk into the chain at `:1822-1830`. **Six `return -1` exits sit AFTER that link** -- `:1964`, `:1980`, `:1991`, `:2074`, `:2088`, `:2099` -- and not one of them unlinks `d`. The most reachable is the plain `fopen` failure at `:1984-1991`: a disk whose file cannot be opened is left on `machine->first_diskimage` with `d->f == NULL`. **What makes it clearly unintended rather than a design choice: the PRE-link failures clean up correctly.** `:1803` does `free(d)` before the link exists. So the function frees on early failure and leaks-onto-the-list on late failure -- the split falling exactly at the link point, which is the signature of checks added after the link rather than of a decision. *** BUT IT IS NOT OBSERVABLE, AND THE CENSUS IS COMPLETE RATHER THAN SAMPLED. *** `grep -rnw diskimage_add` over `src/` returns **8 references, of which exactly TWO are calls**: * `main.c:707` -- on `< 0` prints `Aborting.` and `return 1` (`:708-709`), with NO disk cleanup between; * `emul_parse.c:558` -- on `< 0` calls **`exit(1)`** (`:561`). **Both terminate the process immediately.** There is no debugger or runtime path that adds a disk to a live machine (0 hits in `src/core/debugger*.c`), so the stale entry cannot outlive the call. **The one second-order route was checked and is also closed:** a shutdown walker would dereference the half-built entry (`d->f == NULL`). `atexit` appears **once** in the whole tree -- `emul.c:913`, `atexit(fix_console)` -- which restores terminal state and never touches the disk chain. *That check is the reason this is recorded as latent rather than as a possible NULL dereference at exit.* **DISPOSITION: TRUE, LATENT, NOT FIXED.** Unlinking on the late failures is a few lines and would be tidier, but the addition licence wants a measured delta or a transferred warrant and there is neither: the entry is unreachable by construction, so no row could redden on it and no detector could be built that is not vacuous. **It becomes live the moment any caller survives a failed add** -- that is the trigger to re-open this, and it is the thing to check in any round that adds a runtime disk-attach path. closed

The measuring seat REPRODUCED the SIGFPE and core dump directly. *** R4'S OWN CLAMP MADE IT REACHABLE SOONER: *** before #427/#428 a zero load gave freq=+INF, interval=0.0 and a catch-up loop that never advanced -- a guest-reachable HANG inside SIGALRM, so the machine froze before the division could run. (1) THE ASan CLAIM: refuted on its premise, upheld on its conclusion, and a THIRD reason found that neither I nor the reporting seat had. build_asan.sh:38-39 does set -fsanitize=address,undefined, and the artifact carries eleven __ubsan_handle_* imports INCLUDING __ubsan_handle_add_overflow -- the exact handler an int++ overflow calls. So 'no -fsanitize flag' is false; the seat had grepped the CONSUMER (gate_asan_sweep.sh) rather than the PRODUCER. *** But gate 9 still cannot catch this, and the reason I gave (timeout 25 vs a 42.95 s floor) was only half of it: DEVINIT(footbridge) NEVER CREATES A struct timer AT ALL. *** Only a guest write to TIMER_x_LOAD or TIMER_x_CONTROL|ENABLE does, and a construction sweep runs no guest -- so timer_tick0 is never called and the counter never increments, timeout or no timeout. Either reason alone is fatal. (2) THE '~7.9 s FOR FOUR TIMERS' FIGURE: confirmed impossible, and the seat found WHERE THE NUMBER CAME FROM, which is better than refuting it. 2^31 / (4 x 1048576 x 65) = 7.876 s -- the single-element floor divided by four. The counters are per-timer (:73), each callback increments its own element (:86-92), and the catch-up budget is per-timer too (timer.c:281, inside the per-timer loop), so four timers overflow four DIFFERENT elements at their own rates. True floors: 42.950 s cats (2^31/50,000,000, machine_cats.c:56-57) now measured three times at 43.03/43.10/44.58, and 33.686 s netwinder (2^31/63,750,000, machine_netwinder.c:56). ONE REFINEMENT worth recording: a hard floor of 31.51 s exists from the catch-up ceiling (2^31/68,157,440), but it needs a timer at or above 68.16 MHz, which neither machine's emulated_hz permits. cats's is guarded by `if (== 0)` so a config-file emulated_hz word could reach it; netwinder's is unconditional. Neither is guest-reachable, so severity is unchanged. — evidence: build_asan.sh:38-39; nm of /tmp/gx-asan-head/gxemul; timer.c:281; machine_cats.c:56-57·······

Told to build the single-overlay row a prior pass had specified, it built that, then probed two SIBLING mutants and measured that the single-overlay row catches ONLY the deletion: `continue` -> `break;` and `continue` -> `return 0;` both pass it GREEN, because with one overlay there is no next iteration and all three mutants trace identically. A SECOND OVERLAY separates them and one row kills all three. It supplied both patches and recommended the stronger, which also perturbs no existing gate check where the fallback would have forced one from "1" to "2". * Mechanism: __wrap_fsync consults a static fail_fsync_fd, sets errno=EIO and returns -1 without calling __real_fsync; armed after the WRITE, disarmed when the command returns. It rejected, with reasons written into the file, a real failing fsync (needs dm-error/root, non-portable -- same class as the drvfs trap), close()ing the fd under the live FILE* (a FAULT, and can hit a recycled fd) and an O_RDONLY fd (rc 0 on glibc, proves nothing). * A CRASH IS NOT WHAT MAKES IT FAIL, measured four ways: rc is 1 never >=128; the mutant printed all 11 rows plus the verdict line so it reached the end of main; ASan+UBSan produced 0 bytes on both arms; and exactly one row differs, by a printed string. * INSTRUMENT-SABOTAGE CONTROL (`if (0 && fd == fail_fsync_fd)`) turns TWO rows red, so a dead injection fails loudly and the signatures are distinguishable: two red together = the instrument, the ordering row red alone = the code. * VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE MAIN LOOP, and MY FIRST THREE ATTEMPTS WERE ALL VOID -- the loop variable was eaten before reaching WSL and the printed rc was grep's status; then the anchor took 'the first continue in a range' when the loop has TWO and the f_data==NULL branch never executes, so all three mutants 'passed' and would have discredited the row; then anchoring on the fsync call matched :1211 in overlay_set_block_in_use, a different function. Only a context printout of the line about to be mutated caught it. Correctly anchored on the unique 'Data is not durable' comment: ALL THREE MUTANTS KILLED, traces distinguishable -- deleted publishes b0 anyway, break/return0 stop at F(d0) S(d0). * Gate 2: PASS 235 checks (was 231). Honest limits recorded in the file: the CHECK-CONDITION row is a WITNESS not a discriminator (green on every code mutant); an fflush failure on the data file is not injected, only fsync; and the injection skips the real fsync, so a partially-successful sync is UNTESTED and UNKNOWN. wdcnoirqwdcnoirq wdc_command()'s default: arm asserts no interrupt, so an interrupt-driven guest waits for a completion that never comesAwdcnoirq wdc_command()'s default: arm asserts no interrupt, so an interrupt-driven guest waits for a completion that never comes — commits: d819188 — HOLD: held for the regress seat -- see the entry note and fable_queue.md — Two statements, two arms. Detector 128 rows with one row of eight legs; the floor was breached twice on pass 2 (M10 at the SEC arm, and D1..D5 from the task file being zero on every leg) and closed in-round both times. Gate PASS 334. Witness `detector:` with the rung-3 attempt recorded at BELIEVED; a rebuild is in flight and on green this re-witnesses to `probe:`. — witness: probe:regress/artifacts/wdcnoirq/witness_20260827/wdcnoirq_rung3_probe.py -- rung-3, with RESULTS.txt, rows_pre/post.out and transcript_pre/post.log preserved beside it. *** REPOINTED 2026-08-28: this field cited _scratchpad/witness485/, a volatile path. The files were still there and are now copied into the repo -- the FOURTH instance of the volatile-path class, found while repairing the third (wdcoddstep). *** — note: *** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE and GUEST-REACHABLE. It is the SAME DEFECT SHAPE as [[b120]] in a different device family, which is the part worth carrying. *** With an IDE disk attached, `wdc_command()`'s `default:` arm sets `WDCE_ABRT` but **never sets `int_assert`**, and `dev_wdc_tick()` raises the IRQ only when that latch is set. So an unsupported command is refused **without the completion interrupt an interrupt-driven guest is waiting for.** > *** THE FAMILY: an unsupported command's `default:` arm omits the COMPLETION SIGNAL the guest is blocked on. *** [[b120]] is the SCSI form -- no status byte, so the guest is told GOOD. This is the IDE form -- no interrupt, so the guest is told nothing at all. **Two device families, one omission.** Whichever is fixed first should be checked against the other, and the reviewer question generalises: *does this `default:` arm complete the protocol, or only decline the command?* **Guest-reachable** (seat cites an existing record, not re-run): on landisk, clear any prior IRQ with a status read, then write an unsupported command code and wait. **Observable:** guest IRQ delivery -- whether execution reaches the landisk interrupt vector after the refused command. **Honest limit, and the seat stated it rather than hiding it:** the *indefinite guest wait* in the title is REASONED, not observed. The missing IRQ is READ from the source; that it hangs a real driver forever is an inference. Do not carry the hang as measured. closed

CLUSTER PANEL on wdc_command()'s `default:` arm -- five rows, one code path, none of them previously reviewed by anyone but the seat that filed it. *** THE SEATS WERE UNANIMOUS ON THE QUESTION THAT DECIDES THE WORK: SPLIT. *** Four independent verdict lines said so (agy: 'four defects in one arm require three distinct oracles, cross subsystem boundaries'; deepseek: 'one default: arm yields at least three distinct semantic classes/oracles'; minimax: 'the four rows collapse to two distinct fix designs'; glm: 'one arm, three distinct oracles -- host-log count, IRQ assertion, fsync ordering'). The reopening rule's NO-NEW-ORACLE prong is what does the splitting, and the argument is mechanical rather than stylistic: a detector that counts host stderr lines cannot observe int_assert; one that observes int_assert cannot observe fsync ordering; one that observes fsync ordering cannot count log lines. THE AGREED SPLIT: Round A wdcflood alone -- oracle: host-log line count; fix: the warned_* latch idiom, which #337 already applied THREE TIMES in this same file. Assessment (initial problem)✓2026-08-19 — CONFIRMED — *** RULED THIS SHOULD BE ITS OWN ROUND, and the ruling is accepted. *** On the reopening rule's objective prong: a detector for this defect must assert 'SETUP within T seconds', which is a WALL-CLOCK ORACLE -- the class this project's records treat as most dangerous -- and the rule admits a second site only with NO NEW ORACLE. It also rejected the ledger's own grouping argument ('both fixes are a dozen lines together') as a SIZE argument, which is not one of the prongs. Separately it found that `timeout=` as I specified it is not enough for the BUILD phase, and that `start_new_session` is what makes killpg safe -- without it the children share the GATE's process group and killpg is gate suicide. Its stated MECHANISM (a blocking post-kill drain) was measured FALSE on POSIX; the conclusion held for a different reason. — evidence: _scratchpad/panel_20260819_232621/✓2026-08-19 — CONFIRMED — DERIVED THE TIMEOUTS FROM MEASUREMENT rather than choosing them: slowest build across all 12 lanes 1.37 s, slowest run 0.31 s, on an idle machine. Recommends build=120 s (~88x) and run=60 s (~190x), SEPARATE, env-overridable -- separate because the diagnoses differ (a two-minute compile means the host is sick; a spinning run is the EXPECTED mutant outcome) and because the SETUP message must name the phase. On margin it cited this project's own gate_ab, which uses 3x and measurably false-FAILed a 45-minute battery under load, so 3x is KNOWN-INSUFFICIENT here. It measured the process-group kill both ways: run(timeout=) returned at 3.00 s and left the spinner alive; Popen(start_new_session)+killpg reaped the whole tree, child pgid 32 against the gate's 11, so killpg provably cannot reach the gate. It also found THREE MORE no-token paths with no hang at all -- a subject path typo, a missing fragment file, a wrong argument count -- each a traceback with no token, and noted that `if not failtok` printed FAIL even when stdout had NO token, a case gate_offline.sh:913-925 records being measured before and which was fixed in two detectors rather than in the helper. — evidence: _scratchpad/panel_20260819_232621/✓2026-08-20 — MANUAL — WALL DISCHARGED -- re-fired 2026-08-20 after codex answered a health test (CODEX_ALIVE_20260820, and it got the arithmetic right). The entire domain idata >= 32769 collapses to hz = 0, which timer_clamp_freq then floors SILENTLY to 1e-8 Hz: one tick per 3.17 years. *** A GUEST ASKING FOR 0.5 Hz GETS A TIMER THAT NEVER FIRES. *** Not 'lands below the floor' -- destroyed BEFORE timer.c ever sees it. Flooring 0 -> 1e-8 in timer.c is CORRECT; a floor complaint there would make this noisier while still wrong. RUNG-3 WITNESS BUILT TODAY, two subtypes, unmodified in-tree machine, no device_add, every planted word disassembled and text-compared before stepping: hpcmips/z50 (VR4121) cold debugger, no boot LIVENESS idata=0x00008000 -> [ vr41xx: rtc interrupts at 1 Hz ] control green SUBJECT idata=0x00010000 -> [ vr41xx: rtc interrupts at 0 Hz ] guest asked 0.5 Hz Identical on mobilepro770. Both required controls present: liveness AND device signature ((vr41xx@0xb000000)+0xd0 plus the device's own message -- RAM produces no line at all). The encoding guard earned its keep: the first run REFUSED a verdict because the expected mnemonic strings were wrong, and reported SETUP rather than passing. TWO OTHER LEGS MEASURED, one FALSE: *** footbridge is REFUTED *** -- bounded below by emulated_hz / 2^32, so emulated_hz would have to be < 42.95 Hz; on a 33 MHz machine the worst case is 0.0077 Hz, six orders of magnitude above the floor. The jazz leg is much weaker than filed: 64-bit store only (any 32-bit store bottoms out at 2.33e-7 Hz, 23x above floor). THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME DEFECT, WHICH DOES MERGE: dev_vr41xx.c:614 `case 0xd2: /* RTCL1_H_REG_W */ break;` is a NO-OP. vr_rtcreg.h:87-88 names RTCL1_L/H_REG_W as the halves of a 32-bit reload, so the high half is silently discarded -- and since L is 16 bits, THE SUB-1-Hz DOMAIN IS EXACTLY THE DOMAIN THAT NEEDS H. Same device, same class, same oracle, one fix design. Does NOT merge with n4/#429 despite both being 'a guest rate narrowed': different device, OPPOSITE END of the domain, different mechanism (wide-domain ceiling vs integer-division floor collapse), new oracle. — evidence: rung-3 probe on hpcmips/z50 + mobilepro770; dev_vr41xx.c:606,614·······

Two full LSB/MSB pairs after one mode write produced THREE recomputes -- 97 Hz, **0 Hz**, 97 Hz -- where hardware does two. TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the first is what makes it matter: it transiently drives the counter to ZERO, i.e. straight into the i8253zero defect, FROM A GUEST THAT NEVER PROGRAMS COUNT 0. That inverts the reachability finding on i8253zero, where no available guest asks for count 0 directly. Second: if the second pair's LSB is nonzero it is SILENTLY LOST -- intending 0x3055 the device holds 0x3000. Same device and the same semantic class as i8253zero (counter-load byte routing), so it is the natural companion if a round takes a second site. — evidence: _scratchpad/t8253/ (pit8253_count0_probe.py, pit8253_site_probe.py)✓2026-08-20 — MANUAL — WALL DISCHARGED -- re-fired 2026-08-20 after codex answered a health test (CODEX_ALIVE_20260820, and it got the arithmetic right). The file's own header carries the author's TODO at line 35: '(Split counter[] into reset value and current value.)' So d->counter[] is the PROGRAMMED RELOAD VALUE, FROZEN. gxemul models the timer's RATE (timer_add / timer_update_frequency) and its INTERRUPTS, but never a counting register. WHY THAT REFRAMES THE FIX: OpenBSD's microtime() latches and reads the counter to INTERPOLATE SUB-TICK TIME. If a 'correct' latch returns a constant, the guest's interpolated time does not advance within a tick -- a different wrong answer from 0, and arguably a WORSE one because it is plausible rather than obviously broken. So the candidate that looks most correct (return the programmed value) may be the one that misleads a guest furthest, and the honest round may be smaller than the row implies: make the latch not-an-error and not-a-flood, and DOCUMENT that sub-tick interpolation is unmodelled. sh4pclocksh4pclock One guest TCR store ends the host on THREE machine types (hpcsh, baresh, testsh) -- the sh4 device is added by the CPU, but only 2 of 5 arch-4 SH machines set pclockAsh4pclock One guest TCR store ends the host on THREE machine types (hpcsh, baresh, testsh) -- the sh4 device is added by the CPU, but only 2 of 5 arch-4 SH machines set pclock — commits: 0bb8be2 2965aa1 — *** THE DEFECT IS A CLASS, AND THE FIX IS AT THE GUARD FOR THAT REASON. *** cpu_sh.c:233-234 adds the sh4 device from `arch == 4`, so THE CPU BRINGS THE TMU AND THE BOARD BRINGS THE CLOCK, and nothing checked that the two agree. Five registered SH machine types name an arch-4 CPU; only machine_dreamcast.c:51 and machine_landisk.c:81 assign pclock. Fixing the three machine files would leave every FUTURE arch-4 machine inheriting the same host kill. THE ROW'S TITLE SAID 'hpcsh AND testsh' AND THAT UNDERCOUNTS. Two pass-1 seats independently found that machine_test.c:535 is MACHINE_DEFAULT_CPU(baresh) and :541 is MACHINE_DEFAULT_CPU(testsh) -- two separately registered machines in one file -- so `baresh` was never named by the brief or the filing. Measured: it dies identically. THREE machine types, not two. A seat also measured -e jornada690 reproducing (the subtype is never read; same code path) and confirmed all five machines carry the device. THE FIX follows #447's precedent twenty lines below in the same arm, and its stated reason: 'substituting a prescaler for a clock source we cannot provide would be inventing a rate'. Once-only diagnostic, break, no state touched, using the ELEVENTH SH4_VAL_* latch class -- free, because the tenth-class enum conversion was already discharged. The guard STAYS ABOVE the prescaler switch: run it lower and timer_hz is already set from `idata & 3`, so with pclock == 0 the debug() line announces 'clock set to 0.000000 Hz'. `m_below` measures exactly that and is caught by `unlatch` alone. DE-ESCALATION CLAUSE DISCHARGED BY MEASURED KILL. The predicate that gated death is exactly one, and a seat established it was THE LAST GUEST-REACHABLE exit( IN THE DEVICE (one wrapped in #ifdef SH4_DEBUG, three on interrupt_handler_lookup construction failures; LINE NUMBERS OMITTED DELIBERATELY -- an earlier draft cited four and the paragraph correcting the false panel claim shifted every one of them, which is the finding: a comment citing line numbers in its own file invalidates them when edited). Four accept rows across TWO machines and TWO channels each -- a single row pinned at landisk's 33.33 MHz is passed by a mutant that HARDCODES 33333333, and dreamcast's 50 MHz is the discriminator. They redden under a guard-only growth mutant `|| (pclock % 256) != 0`; guard-only is the correct form by the #451 discriminator because THE LATCH OPERAND IS THE CONSTANT 1, which the guard cannot feed. THE HONEST COST HAS TWO HALVES, and the round demoted the first too far before two seats corrected it. (a) The STALL remains the primary behavioural cost, and for automation it turns an immediate nonzero exit into a possible timeout. (b) ADDITIONALLY the diagnostic degrades from unmissable to once-per-timer. (b) does not replace (a). What narrows (a)'s practical reach today: hpcsh's MACHINE_SETUP has its hpc_bootinfo half commented out at :48-64 -- the live body still registers RAM mirrors and a framebuffer -- so with no console wiring, no bootinfo and no disk NO OS BOOTS THERE. Note the stall is only hypothetical ON HPCSH: baresh and testsh run hand-written test programs, and a program that programs TCR and polls TCNT IS the hang. This detector plants exactly such a program; what actually degrades is the diagnostic, from unmissable to once-per-timer-for-the-device-lifetime. *** THE ROUND SHIPPED A FALSE CLAIM ABOUT ITS OWN PANEL AND THE MISCOUNTED SEAT CAUGHT IT. *** An early draft of the shipped comment said 'a panel of nine seats reached this 8-1'; it was written WHILE THE NINTH SEAT WAS STILL RUNNING and that seat then did not vote B. Corrected in place. Accurate: all nine answered, ALL NINE AGREE THE DECLINE IS MANDATORY, seven say it is the whole fix, two would additionally give the SYNTHETIC machines a defined pclock -- filed as sh4testclock, not merged, per the round-scope rule. CORRECTED AFTER THE CODE COMMIT, by pass 2: the guard-placement claim cited #447's silent-wrong-rate hazard, which CANNOT OCCUR AT THIS PREDICATE -- pclock == 0 makes every prescaler case 0.0 and timer_hz[] is already 0.0 from the DEVINIT memset. The placement is still right, for diagnostic consistency (the debug() line is unlatched and would print per-STORE). And `m_below` was misattributed to that claim: it is the missing-`break` mutant caught by `unlatch`, and NOTHING in the kill table measures the guard's position. Also: the read-back channel is itself a FABRICATION -- real SH-4 always latches TCR, so a guest doing read-modify-write silently loses its update, and `unlatch` pins that as correct. It is the lesser of two fabrications, not an architectural channel, and the record now says so. — witness: probe:regress/sh_pclock_probe.py (rung 3, 16 rows, SHIPPED). But the reopening rule prices 'no new oracle', and reaching :334 needed a new opcode, a new loop shape and a new state manipulation. Meanwhile `curl -s localhost:11434/api/tags` lists **`kimi-k3:cloud` as LIVE**, and three earlier panels (`panel_20260824_191634`, `panel_20260824_231824`, `panel_20260825_000248`) each hold an `ollama_kimi.txt`, so the seat was being fired BY HAND and then stopped being. *** SO THE HONEST STATUS OF THIS SEAT IS NOT "DOWN". *** kimi's CLI transport is walled; kimi itself is reachable and idle. Every panel since the CLI wall has silently run one seat short while a working transport sat unused -- which is the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape with an extra step, because here the roster does not even record a failure to investigate. RECOVERED IMMEDIATELY: the seat was fired by hand onto the live `wdcflood` pass-1 panel dir as `ollama_kimi.txt`. FIX OWED IN panel.sh, deliberately NOT APPLIED YET because panel.sh was RUNNING when this was found and bash reads a script incrementally -- editing a running script is its own defect class. The fix: fire `kimi-k3:cloud` as a fourth Ollama seat, and have the seat check report the CLI wall and the substitute SEPARATELY so a walled transport with a live substitute reads as one seat answered, not as a loss. Also correct `429` to the actual status text rather than a hardcoded code. *** AND THE GENERAL RULE THIS EARNS: WHEN A SEAT WALLS, ASK WHETHER THE MODEL IS REACHABLE BY ANOTHER TRANSPORT BEFORE RECORDING IT DOWN. *** The carrier already separates a wall from a refused connection; this is the third class -- **one transport walled, another live** -- and it is the only one where the seat is available the whole time and nobody asks.closed

That is the documented two-step, not a defect. *** FIXED 2026-08-26: one character, `x` added to the negative lookbehind. *** `check_score_claims.py` now reads `(?<![\dx/])(\d+)\s*/\s*(\d+)(?![\d/%])`. The `00` in `0x00/0x10` is preceded by `x`, which the old `(?<![\d/])` allowed, so a slash-separated HEX LIST parsed as a score claim. **NEGATIVE-CONTROLLED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS BEFORE LANDING, which is the whole discipline for a regex change:** five real score claims (13/13, 26/26, 8/32, "52 / 52", 16/16) all still match; two hex lists no longer do; zero regressions. **AND MEASURED ON THE FILE THAT PRODUCED THE ORIGINAL FALSE FAIL** rather than on synthetic strings: over the whole of `asic_badaddr_probe.py` the old regex found 11 matches and the new one finds 7. **The four killed are `04/4`, `08/4`, `10/4`, `18/4` -- every one a fragment of a hex offset. The kept are `12/12` and `12/13` -- every real claim, intact.** *** COVERAGE VERIFIED NOT TO HAVE SHRUNK, because 'the false positive is gone' and 'the checker stopped looking' produce the same output: *** the gate still carries 12 rows naming the probe, the checker still reports SCORE_CLAIMS_PASS over 19 pinned probes, and the docstring still yields its 5 genuine `12/13` claims under BOTH regexes. A fix that silently drops a probe from coverage would have read as success. *The row's own diagnosis was correct and complete; nothing in it needed revising. Worth noting because most rows worked today needed their evidence corrected -- this one was filed right the first time.* MEASURED 2026-08-25 during #463's pre-commit. Section U reported THREE stale score claims in `asic_badaddr_probe.py`'s docstring -- `claims 00/0`, `10/0`, `20/0`, pin is 12. **None of them was ever written.** All three come from ONE line of ordinary prose: `bases 0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30`, a slash-separated list of hex group bases. The pattern `(?<![\d/])(\d+)\s*/\s*(\d+)(?![\d/%])` sees `0x00/0x10` and takes `00` / `0`. *** IT IS A FALSE FAIL, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE FAILURE FROM THE ONE SECTION U EXISTS TO CATCH, AND IS STILL EXPENSIVE. *** A gate that reddens on prose trains its reader to explain away red rows, which is exactly how a REAL stale score would then get waved through. And this project writes `0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30` constantly -- the fourth-word invariant is naturally expressed that way -- so it will recur in any file section U checks. WORKED AROUND, NOT FIXED, and deliberately: #463 reworded its own docstring to use commas, because the round's material is unshipped (L1) while `check_score_claims.py` is a shared gate and editing it is a different scope. **The workaround is also the weaker fix** -- it relies on every future author avoiding a natural notation. THE REAL FIX is one lookbehind: reject a match whose left digit run is preceded by `0x` or `0X`, i.e. require the numerator not be part of a hex literal. Note the existing escape hatch (`write '<N>-row' on the same line`) does NOT help here, because the denominator the checker invented is 0 and nobody would write `0-row`.closed

ONE round -- the coupling makes them one repair, and shipping half is worse than shipping neither; 2. TWO rounds, re-arm FIRST -- fix the truthfulness defect, then bound the push on a re-arm that works; 3. ONE round bounding the push AND accepting the stall, filing the re-arm -- **rejected on its face**: it knowingly ships a hang. *Recorded before any edit.
